project.name: ccp
project.description: Compliance companion platform: a teaching-scale reference build of an AI-native compliance automation platform on production technology, covering connectors, normalization and identity resolution, evaluators with verified citations, a bitemporal compliance-state table, and agents behind a human approval stage.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the ccp (compliance companion platform) package; it holds only a docstring pointing readers to spec.md for the design.

nodes.name: cli.py
nodes.summary: Typer sub-app for `ccp agent` that lists pending and recent graph threads, inspects interrupts, resumes a thread through the approval stage with a signed-in reviewer's decision, replays recorded tier 3 runs, lints the tool policy, and reports or gates harness metrics per release bundle.

nodes.name: pending
nodes.summary: CLI command listing agent threads stopped at the human gate, with their interrupt draft details and last update time.

nodes.name: list_threads
nodes.summary: CLI command printing recent agent threads of every status, including each trajectory as an arrow-joined path.

nodes.name: inspect
nodes.summary: CLI command showing one thread's interrupt payload and recorded trajectory after checking the thread belongs to the requested tenant.

nodes.name: resume
nodes.summary: CLI command that authenticates a member's token, records their decision (approve, override or regather) on the thread's open approval item, then resumes the graph from that record and persists the resulting verdict.

nodes.name: replay
nodes.summary: CLI command that re-runs a recorded tier 3 run from its run log alone and exits 1 on the first model request the log does not hold.

nodes.name: lint
nodes.summary: CLI command running the Rule-of-Two lint over the agent tool policy, exiting 1 when one principal could read untrusted content, hold private data and change state.

nodes.name: harness_report
nodes.summary: CLI command printing harness metrics per graph and release bundle, plus how fanned-out task reads went, as JSON.

nodes.name: harness_gate
nodes.summary: CLI command that compares a candidate release bundle against a baseline and refuses it (exit 1) when its runs end in loop or cap stops more often.

nodes.name: decisions.py
nodes.summary: Fail-closed reviewer decisions on tier 3 interrupts: builds and validates decisions, records each with a queued apply job in one transaction, applies them through the `applies` topic consumer with retry, and audits decisions left unapplied or applied without a record.

nodes.name: InvalidDecision
nodes.summary: ValueError raised for a decision that names no known action, no reviewer, or no valid override status.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: The only constructor of a reviewer decision: validates the action (approve, override, regather), reviewer and override status, and never defaults an unknown action to approve.

nodes.name: validate
nodes.summary: Re-checks a decision arriving from storage or a caller with the same rules as build.

nodes.name: DecisionOutcome
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass holding the result of applying a decision: the approval item, the resulting verdict, whether it was inserted, and any error; reports whether the graph resumed.

nodes.name: _resume_and_commit
nodes.summary: Resumes the tier 3 graph from an item's recorded decision and commits the resulting verdict through the evaluations runner.

nodes.name: _apply
nodes.summary: Applies a recorded decision; a failure leaves the decision recorded and the thread failed so that retry can pick it up.

nodes.name: queue_apply
nodes.summary: Appends the apply job for an approval item to the event log inside the decision's own transaction.

nodes.name: ApplyJobs
nodes.summary: ParallelConsumer on the `applies` topic that applies each recorded tier 3 decision once: skips applied items, treats payload mismatches as terminal, retries other failures, and lets the deciding process act as the job's first worker via apply_now.

nodes.name: decide
nodes.summary: Records a signed-in member's decision on an open tier 3 item after checking the payload is still the pending interrupt, queues its apply job in the same transaction, then applies it immediately.

nodes.name: retry
nodes.summary: Re-applies a recorded decision after a failed resume, still verifying the payload is the pending interrupt so a stale decision cannot reach a later interrupt.

nodes.name: is_applied
nodes.summary: Reports whether an item's decision took effect: its thread finished with a stored verdict, or a regather sent it back to the gate where a newer item waits.

nodes.name: unapplied
nodes.summary: Lists decided tier 3 items whose threads have not finished with a stored verdict.

nodes.name: audit
nodes.summary: Finds finished tier 3 threads that applied a decision no reviewer recorded on an approval item.

nodes.name: threads.py
nodes.summary: Data access for the agent_threads table, one row per graph run: creates threads under a release bundle, stores the starting input for replay, transitions status (running, interrupted, finished, cancelled, failed) and lists pending or recent threads.

nodes.name: ThreadRow
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass mirroring an agent_threads row: graph, test, subject, status, interrupt payload, decision, verdict id, error and trajectory with timestamps.

nodes.name: _row
nodes.summary: Maps a database tuple to a ThreadRow, decoding its JSON columns.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Inserts a new thread row for a graph run under the given release bundle id, or the process's current bundle.

nodes.name: set_input
nodes.summary: Stores the initial state a run started from, once, so a replay can start it again.

nodes.name: input_of
nodes.summary: Reads the stored initial input of a thread.

nodes.name: resumable
nodes.summary: Finds the newest thread for an evaluation that stopped without an outcome, so a retry continues it instead of starting over.

nodes.name: mark_running
nodes.summary: Sets a thread's status to running.

nodes.name: mark_interrupted
nodes.summary: Marks a thread interrupted at the human gate, storing its interrupt payload and trajectory.

nodes.name: mark_finished
nodes.summary: Marks a thread finished with its verdict id, trajectory and the decision it applied.

nodes.name: mark_cancelled
nodes.summary: Marks a thread cancelled by a person with the reason; its record stays and nothing it would have decided is decided.

nodes.name: mark_failed
nodes.summary: Marks a thread failed with its error and trajectory.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Fetches one thread row by id.

nodes.name: pending
nodes.summary: Lists threads currently interrupted at the human gate.

nodes.name: all_threads
nodes.summary: Lists recent threads of every status, up to a limit.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package docstring for the HTTP API: FastAPI over the same services the CLI uses, with server-verified bearer tokens, path-scoped tenants and role checks, and no business rules of its own.

nodes.name: app.py
nodes.summary: FastAPI application exposing the /v1 REST API: health and identity, tenant onboarding, the approvals inbox and decisions, findings and framework reports, remediation proposals and fix suggestions, autonomy levels, method cards, auditor grants and workspace, exceptions, members, tenant settings and the agent tool surface, mapping service errors to HTTP status codes.
nodes.languageNotes: FastAPI dependency injection (Depends) resolves the signed-in principal and tenant Session per request; Pydantic models constrain request bodies, and an ERRORS table maps domain exceptions to HTTP status codes in one place.

nodes.name: Session
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass for a signed-in member acting in one tenant: settings, scoped DB, principal, role and connection pools.

nodes.name: Decide
nodes.summary: Pydantic request body for approving an item: the 64-character payload hash shown, an optional note, the decision (approve, override, regather) and an override status.

nodes.name: NewTenant
nodes.summary: Pydantic request body for onboarding a tenant: id, display name, GitHub org and time zone.

nodes.name: NewException
nodes.summary: Pydantic request body for requesting a control exception: test, subject, end date, reason and owner.

nodes.name: Grant
nodes.summary: Pydantic request body for granting tenant membership: issuer, subject, role and optional email and name.

nodes.name: LevelBody
nodes.summary: Pydantic request body for setting the autonomy level of a workflow's decision class, with a reason.

nodes.name: GrantBody
nodes.summary: Pydantic request body for granting an auditor read access to named audit packages for a number of days.

nodes.name: principal
nodes.summary: FastAPI dependency that extracts the bearer token from the Authorization header and authenticates it into a Principal.

nodes.name: session
nodes.summary: FastAPI dependency that resolves the path tenant and the caller's membership role into a Session, refusing non-members.

nodes.name: me
nodes.summary: GET /v1/me: returns the caller's identity and every tenant where they hold a role.

nodes.name: onboard
nodes.summary: POST /v1/tenants: onboards a new tenant and makes the caller its admin.

nodes.name: inbox
nodes.summary: GET the tenant's approvals inbox, filterable by open state and kind, flagging expired items.

nodes.name: item
nodes.summary: GET one approval item with its payload, hash, expiry and event history.

nodes.name: approve
nodes.summary: POST approve on an approval item with the payload hash the caller was shown, delegating to the approval actions.

nodes.name: reject
nodes.summary: POST reject on an approval item with the shown payload hash and a required note.

nodes.name: break_glass
nodes.summary: POST break-glass approval of an urgent item by an admin, with a reason.

nodes.name: findings
nodes.summary: GET the current compliance-state head of every subject, labelled with any active exception.

nodes.name: report
nodes.summary: GET the framework rollup for one framework, loading the knowledge graph and reading through the read pool.

nodes.name: proposal_list
nodes.summary: GET remediation proposals, optionally filtered by status, each described by the remediation runner.

nodes.name: proposal
nodes.summary: GET one remediation proposal with its description.

nodes.name: dry_run
nodes.summary: POST a dry run (live=False) of a remediation proposal through the remediation runner, returning the mode, detail and planned call; needs a reviewer.

nodes.name: fix_list
nodes.summary: GET fix suggestions, filterable by status and test.

nodes.name: fix
nodes.summary: GET one fix suggestion by id.

nodes.name: _fix_decision
nodes.summary: Shared handler that records a member's accept or dismiss decision on a fix suggestion with a note.

nodes.name: fix_metrics
nodes.summary: GET acceptance metrics for fix suggestions.

nodes.name: autonomy_level
nodes.summary: POST that sets the autonomy level for a workflow's decision class with a reason (admin only), answering 409 when the level is refused.

nodes.name: verdict_card
nodes.summary: GET the method card for one verdict.

nodes.name: fix_card
nodes.summary: GET the method card for one fix suggestion.

nodes.name: auditor_grant
nodes.summary: POST that grants an auditor time-boxed read access to audit packages, judged under the publication policy against their sealed copies.

nodes.name: auditor_revoke
nodes.summary: POST that revokes an auditor grant with a reason.

nodes.name: _workspace
nodes.summary: Dependency for the auditor workspace: an auditor need not be a tenant member; what they may see is decided by their live grants.

nodes.name: auditor_packages
nodes.summary: GET the audit packages an auditor may currently read, with summaries.

nodes.name: auditor_file
nodes.summary: GET one file of an audit package from its sealed copy for an auditor with a live grant; the read is logged.

nodes.name: evidence_feedback
nodes.summary: GET what code (and, once calibrated, the adequacy verifier) said about an evidence upload.

nodes.name: exception_list
nodes.summary: GET every stored control exception with whether it still holds.

nodes.name: exception_ask
nodes.summary: POST a request for a control exception on one failing subject, opening an approval item.

nodes.name: exception_revoke
nodes.summary: POST that ends a control exception early with a reason.

nodes.name: member_list
nodes.summary: GET the tenant's current members and roles.

nodes.name: member_grant
nodes.summary: PUT that grants or changes a member's role (admin only), refusing to demote the last admin.

nodes.name: member_revoke
nodes.summary: DELETE that ends a membership (admin only), refusing to remove the last admin.

nodes.name: settings_show
nodes.summary: GET the tenant's effective settings version.

nodes.name: settings_change
nodes.summary: PATCH that asks for a tenant settings change: applied at once, or, for a change of scope, opened as an approval item that waits for an approver (202).

nodes.name: _tools
nodes.summary: Bridges the agent REST tool surface: builds providers and passes the caller, method, path and body to the agent REST handler.

nodes.name: create_app
nodes.summary: Application factory that builds the FastAPI app over settings, registering the /v1 router, the UI and error handlers, and opening (or sharing) app and agent connection pools for its lifespan.

nodes.name: reasons.py
nodes.summary: Maps reason codes for statuses other than pass or fail (pending, parked, stale and similar) to a plain explanation and the one action that clears each, keeping unknown codes visible with a generic next action.

nodes.name: Reason
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass pairing a reason code with what it says and the next action that clears it.

nodes.name: for_pending
nodes.summary: Looks up the Reason for a pending code, falling back to a generic reason for an unknown code.

nodes.name: for_events
nodes.summary: Turns a verdict's events into Reasons in order, keeping the code of any unknown event.

nodes.name: ui.py
nodes.summary: Server-rendered Jinja UI: dev-issuer and OIDC/PKCE sign-in, tenant home, approval inbox and decisions with CSRF checks, findings with reason codes, framework reports, verdict pages, and live agent run views with streamed steps and stop requests.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses FastAPI with Jinja2 templates for server-side rendering, cookie sessions, a CSRF token derived by hashing the session token, and an OIDC authorization-code flow with PKCE built from hashlib and secrets.

nodes.name: SignIn
nodes.summary: Exception signalling no valid session; it is handled by sending the browser to sign in.

nodes.name: viewer
nodes.summary: FastAPI dependency resolving the signed-in principal from the session cookie.

nodes.name: Page
nodes.summary: A signed-in member's view of one tenant: resolves their role, renders templates with shared context, and checks CSRF tokens and minimum roles on form posts.

nodes.name: login
nodes.summary: GET /ui/login: renders the dev sign-in form offline, or starts an OIDC authorization-code flow with PKCE and a state cookie.

nodes.name: login_dev
nodes.summary: POST /ui/login: mints a dev-issuer token for a subject (dev auth mode only) and signs the browser in.

nodes.name: callback
nodes.summary: GET /ui/callback: checks the state, exchanges the authorization code with the PKCE verifier at the token endpoint, authenticates the returned token and sets the session.

nodes.name: _signed_in
nodes.summary: Sets the session cookie (secure when served over https) and redirects to the UI home.

nodes.name: logout
nodes.summary: POST /ui/logout: clears the session cookie.

nodes.name: home
nodes.summary: GET /ui/: lists the tenants where the signed-in principal holds a role.

nodes.name: _undo
nodes.summary: Says how an approval item's effect is undone, from its payload's risk note or a default per item kind.

nodes.name: inbox
nodes.summary: Renders the tenant's open approval items with payload, hash, expiry and how each is undone.

nodes.name: decide
nodes.summary: POST handler for approve, reject or request-changes from the inbox form, after CSRF and role checks, delegating to the approval actions.

nodes.name: findings
nodes.summary: Renders each subject's status with its exception label and, for anything but pass or fail, reason codes with the action that clears them.

nodes.name: report
nodes.summary: Renders a framework rollup with the reasons behind pending requirements.

nodes.name: verdict
nodes.summary: Renders one verdict with its reasons.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Renders one agent run with its recorded steps and whether a stop was requested.

nodes.name: run_events
nodes.summary: Streams each recorded step of a run as it lands, read from the run log rather than the model's narration, ending when the run ends.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: POST that requests a stop for a running agent thread, after CSRF and role checks.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package docstring for the shared human-in-the-loop approval stage: one table pair, one CLI and one reviewer field for every pause and action, with `store` as data access and `actions` as what approving does.

nodes.name: actions.py
nodes.summary: Defines what approving, rejecting, requesting changes, closing or break-glass approving does for each approval kind (tier 3 interrupts, remediation and rollbacks, exceptions, identity merges, scope changes), failing closed on unseen payloads or invalid decisions.

nodes.name: Outcome
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass returned by approval actions: the updated approval, a human-readable detail, and whether it succeeded.

nodes.name: check_plain_decision
nodes.summary: Refuses a tier 3 style decision or status on any other item kind, so it is never read as a plain approve.

nodes.name: _tier3_outcome
nodes.summary: Turns a tier 3 DecisionOutcome into an Outcome that describes the resumed verdict, or the failure and the command that applies it.

nodes.name: approve
nodes.summary: Approves an item after checking the shown payload hash: tier 3 decisions go through the decisions module, exceptions are minted, scope changes adopt new settings, identity merges link records, and remediation or rollback approvals mint an execution grant.

nodes.name: reject
nodes.summary: Rejects an item: a tier 3 interrupt records an override to needs_review and resumes, an identity merge keeps the records apart, and other kinds record the rejection.

nodes.name: _grant_exception
nodes.summary: Mints a control exception in the approval's transaction from the payload the approver saw, refusing one whose end date has passed.

nodes.name: break_glass
nodes.summary: Lets an admin approve an urgent item they asked for themselves, with a reason; a break_glass_review item then opens for another approver.

nodes.name: resume
nodes.summary: Applies a recorded tier 3 decision whose resume failed.

nodes.name: request_changes
nodes.summary: Records a request-changes event on an item by a signed-in member.

nodes.name: cli.py
nodes.summary: Typer CLI for `ccp approvals` and its exceptions sub-app: list, show, approve, reject, request changes, close, resume, break-glass and audit approval items, and request, list or revoke control exceptions; decisions are proven with sign-in tokens, refusals exit 2 and unapplied decisions exit 1.

nodes.name: list_cmd
nodes.summary: CLI command listing a tenant's approval items, filterable by kind and open state.

nodes.name: show
nodes.summary: CLI command printing one approval item with its payload, hash, expiry and event history.

nodes.name: approve
nodes.summary: CLI command approving an item with a sign-in token, an optional tier 3 decision or status, and the payload hash the reviewer saw.

nodes.name: reject
nodes.summary: CLI command rejecting an item with a sign-in token and a note.

nodes.name: resume
nodes.summary: CLI command applying a recorded tier 3 decision whose resume failed.

nodes.name: request_changes
nodes.summary: CLI command asking for changes on an item with a sign-in token and a note.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: CLI command closing an item, for example an evidence request after the upload.

nodes.name: audit
nodes.summary: CLI command reporting tier 3 decisions recorded but not applied, applied without a record, and break-glass problems; exits 1 on any problem.

nodes.name: break_glass
nodes.summary: CLI command for an admin to approve an urgent item they asked for, with a reason, leaving the use for another approver to review.

nodes.name: exception_request
nodes.summary: CLI command asking for a control exception on one failing subject; another member, an approver, decides it.

nodes.name: exception_list
nodes.summary: CLI command listing stored control exceptions and whether each still holds.

nodes.name: exception_revoke
nodes.summary: CLI command for an approver to end an exception early with a reason.

nodes.name: grants.py
nodes.summary: Single-use execution grants for approved remediation and rollback items: minted in the decision's transaction, bound to the payload and precondition hashes, valid for a day, and consumed exactly once by the executor under a unique key.

nodes.name: GrantUsed
nodes.summary: Raised when a grant was already consumed, so a second use needs a new decision.

nodes.name: Grant
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass for an execution grant bound to an approval, a proposal, a payload hash and a precondition hash, with issue and expiry times; reports whether it expired.

nodes.name: Use
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass recording when a grant was spent and on which operation.

nodes.name: _grant
nodes.summary: Maps a database row to a Grant.

nodes.name: mint
nodes.summary: Inserts one execution grant for an approve decision inside that decision's transaction, valid for a day by default.

nodes.name: for_approval
nodes.summary: Finds the grant minted for an approval item.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Fetches one grant by id.

nodes.name: for_proposal
nodes.summary: Finds the grants minted for a remediation proposal.

nodes.name: use_of
nodes.summary: Reads the recorded use of a grant, if it was spent.

nodes.name: consume
nodes.summary: Spends a grant inside the caller's transaction; of two racing callers the second finds the key taken and raises GrantUsed.

nodes.name: store.py
nodes.summary: Append-only data access for approval items and their events: opens items idempotently, authorizes decisions by role, requester separation and expiry (with admin break-glass), records events with same-transaction side effects such as review labels and execution grants, and queries items, history, labels and break-glass problems.

nodes.name: Expired
nodes.summary: Raised when an item's time to decide has passed; it must be opened again.

nodes.name: AlreadyDecided
nodes.summary: Raised when someone else decided the item first.

nodes.name: payload_hash
nodes.summary: SHA-256 of a payload's canonical JSON, binding a decision to exactly what was shown.

nodes.name: Approval
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass for an approval item's latest state: kind, ref, payload and hash, state, reviewer, decision, requester, expiry, principal and break-glass flag; reports expiry, openness and whether it was decided.

nodes.name: _row
nodes.summary: Maps an approval_status view row to an Approval, decoding JSON columns.

nodes.name: open_item
nodes.summary: Opens an item and records its `opened` event, idempotent per (kind, ref_id) while open and unexpired; the requester may never decide it and it expires after its kind's default.

nodes.name: open_item_in
nodes.summary: Opens a new item inside the caller's transaction, so it exists exactly when what it asks about does (an identity review, a break-glass use).

nodes.name: _break_glass
nodes.summary: The checks a break-glass approval passes in place of separation of duties: an approve event on an urgent item kind by a signed-in admin, an unexpired item, and a daily break-glass limit.

nodes.name: _authorize
nodes.summary: Resolves the principal and role behind an event: a decision needs a signed-in member with the role, who did not ask for it, on an unexpired item, unless an admin breaks the glass.

nodes.name: record_event
nodes.summary: Appends one event by a signed-in member, or by the system for opening and closing, after authorizing it; a `within` callback runs in the same transaction so its writes commit with the event or not at all.

nodes.name: _append_event
nodes.summary: Writes the event row, opens a break_glass_review item for a break-glass use, records every decision as a review label, mints an execution grant for an approved remediation or rollback, and runs the `within` callback, all in one transaction.

nodes.name: labels
nodes.summary: Review labels, oldest first, filtered by consent scope for eval or training use.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Fetches one approval item's current state.

nodes.name: for_ref
nodes.summary: Finds the newest item of a kind for a ref.

nodes.name: items_for_ref
nodes.summary: Every item of one kind for one ref, oldest first.

nodes.name: approved_for
nodes.summary: The newest approved item for exactly this payload hash, so an approval binds to what it showed.

nodes.name: list_items
nodes.summary: Lists items with optional kind and open-only filters.

nodes.name: history
nodes.summary: An item's events in order, with reviewer, note, decision and timestamps.

nodes.name: break_glass_problems
nodes.summary: Break-glass uses a second approver judged unjustified, or left unreviewed past the review's expiry.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Authentication entry point that builds a token Verifier for the configured mode (the dev issuer's keys or the OIDC issuer's published JWKS) and authenticates tokens into Principals, re-exporting the token types.

nodes.name: verifier
nodes.summary: Builds a Verifier that trusts only the dev issuer's in-memory JWKS in dev mode, or only the configured OIDC issuer's remote JWKS in oidc mode.

nodes.name: authenticate
nodes.summary: Returns the Principal a token proves, or raises InvalidToken.

nodes.name: dev_issuer.py
nodes.summary: Local OIDC identity provider for development and tests: an RSA key created on first use in the data directory, its public half as a JWKS document, and ID tokens minted under the dev issuer, never trusted in oidc mode.

nodes.name: private_key
nodes.summary: Loads the dev issuer's RSA private key from the data directory, generating and saving it with restricted permissions on first use.

nodes.name: jwks
nodes.summary: Publishes the dev key's public half as a JWKS document with a SHA-256-derived key id.

nodes.name: mint
nodes.summary: Mints an RS256-signed ID token for a subject with email, name, audience and expiry.

nodes.name: members.py
nodes.summary: Tenant roles decided by CCP, never by a token: append-only versioned membership rows with ranked roles (viewer, reviewer, approver, admin), grant and revoke, current members, role lookup, and a require check that raises NotPermitted.

nodes.name: NotPermitted
nodes.summary: Raised when the principal is not a member of the tenant or its role is too low.

nodes.name: Member
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass for one membership version: identity, role, active flag, who granted it and when; exposes the Principal.

nodes.name: _member
nodes.summary: Maps a tenant_members row to a Member.

nodes.name: _append
nodes.summary: Appends a new membership version for a principal with a role, an active flag and who made the change.

nodes.name: grant
nodes.summary: Makes a principal a member with a role, as a new version rather than an edit.

nodes.name: revoke
nodes.summary: Ends a principal's membership with a new inactive version.

nodes.name: member
nodes.summary: A principal's current membership, read from the current-members view.

nodes.name: current
nodes.summary: Every active member of the tenant.

nodes.name: role_of
nodes.summary: The principal's current role in the tenant, or none.

nodes.name: require
nodes.summary: Returns the principal's role if it ranks at least the one asked for, otherwise raises NotPermitted.

nodes.name: tokens.py
nodes.summary: Server-side OIDC token verification: a Verifier checks the signature against the issuer's keys (static or remote JWKS), accepted asymmetric algorithms only, the issuer, the audience or client_id, and the expiry, yielding an immutable Principal.
nodes.languageNotes: Pins accepted JWT algorithms to asymmetric ones so neither `none` nor an HMAC algorithm keyed with a public key can be smuggled in, a classic JWT algorithm-confusion defence.

nodes.name: InvalidToken
nodes.summary: PermissionError raised when a token cannot be trusted and the request is refused.

nodes.name: Principal
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass identifying a person by issuer and subject, with email and name for display only; provides a stable principal_id and a label.

nodes.name: StaticKeys
nodes.summary: Key source backed by an in-memory JWKS document, for the local dev issuer and tests.

nodes.name: RemoteKeys
nodes.summary: Key source that fetches and caches keys from the issuer's JWKS endpoint, such as Cognito's.

nodes.name: Verifier
nodes.summary: Verifies a JWT: refuses disallowed algorithms, resolves the signing key, checks issuer and expiry, accepts CCP's client in aud or client_id, and returns a Principal.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package docstring for the compliance state read model: the verdicts-topic writer, the reader and the full pipeline run; everything downstream reads state here, never from verdicts.

nodes.name: attest.py
nodes.summary: Attestation record for every assertion CCP makes outside itself: judges items' provenance, completeness and age under the versioned publication policy YAML, and records an attestations row with the policy version, reasons and a digest of what was asserted.

nodes.name: Item
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass for one asserted item: its id, provenance, whether it was assessed, and when it was true.

nodes.name: Decision
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass for an attestation outcome: the attestation id, whether it may go out, the policy version and the reasons.

nodes.name: policy
nodes.summary: Loads and caches the publication policy YAML, returning its content-hash version and per-kind rules.

nodes.name: judge
nodes.summary: Returns the policy version and every reason an item may not go out: no rule for the kind, a provenance the kind forbids, an item too old, or an unassessed item where the kind does not allow incomplete ones.

nodes.name: attest
nodes.summary: Judges an assertion and records one attestations row, allowed or not, with the policy version, reasons and a digest of the content.

nodes.name: provenance_of_result
nodes.summary: Classifies a package result's provenance: a rule over provider data, over uploads, or a model's reading.

nodes.name: auditors.py
nodes.summary: Auditor workspace: time-boxed (at most 90 days), read-only grants to named audit packages, judged and recorded as attestations before they are made, with listing of visible packages and logged file reads from sealed copies.

nodes.name: Grant
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass for an auditor grant: principal, package ids, expiry, grantor and revoked flag.

nodes.name: _package
nodes.summary: Loads an audit package's framework, valid and known times, manifest and sealed file references.

nodes.name: grant
nodes.summary: Judges the share under the publication policy using the results in each package's sealed copy, records the attestation, and grants only what it allows, for at most 90 days.

nodes.name: revoke
nodes.summary: Revokes an auditor grant with a reason.

nodes.name: live_grants
nodes.summary: An auditor's grants that are unrevoked and unexpired now.

nodes.name: visible
nodes.summary: The packages a principal may read now, each with the grant that allows it.

nodes.name: read_file
nodes.summary: Reads one file of a package the principal may see from its sealed copy, logging the read.

nodes.name: package_summary
nodes.summary: A package's framework, valid and known times, and its sealed file names.

nodes.name: exceptions.py
nodes.summary: Asking for and ending control exceptions: a reviewer or above opens an exception approval item for one failing subject (reason, owner, end date at most a year out), another member approves it, and an approver may end it early; no verdict is changed.

nodes.name: NotExceptable
nodes.summary: Raised when the subject is not failing or the request is incomplete.

nodes.name: request
nodes.summary: Opens an exception approval item for one failing subject after checking role, the current failing state and the end date, with a payload naming the failing verdict; returns its approval id.

nodes.name: revoke
nodes.summary: Ends an exception early, an approver's call recorded with the reason.

nodes.name: reader.py
nodes.summary: Compliance state reader API: thin wrappers over bitemporal current, believed and as-of state, chains and heads, plus the coverage-aware framework rollup, status counts and row formatting with exception labels.

nodes.name: current_state
nodes.summary: A subject's current compliance state row.

nodes.name: believed_state
nodes.summary: What CCP believed a subject's state was at a given time.

nodes.name: state_as_of
nodes.summary: A subject's state valid at one time as known at another (bitemporal as-of query).

nodes.name: chain
nodes.summary: Every state row of a subject in order.

nodes.name: heads
nodes.summary: The current head row of every subject.

nodes.name: framework_rollup
nodes.summary: Rolls a framework up over the expected population, so an unassessed, parked or stale subject is pending rather than a pass, with exceptions annotated.

nodes.name: StatusCounts
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass of subject counts by status, with whether no evaluations exist yet.

nodes.name: status_counts
nodes.summary: Counts current heads by status.

nodes.name: format_row
nodes.summary: Formats a state row as a one-line summary with valid and recorded times and any exception label.

nodes.name: run.py
nodes.summary: Runs the whole idempotent pipeline for one tenant: ingest fixtures, normalize, resolve identities, refresh the retrieval index, enqueue and drain evaluations, and write compliance state, returning a RunReport.

nodes.name: RunReport
nodes.summary: Dataclass of a pipeline run's counts: landed, duplicates, normalized, identities compared, chunks, enqueued, evaluated, parked, statuses, state rows written by reason, AI tier availability and heads.

nodes.name: Prepared
nodes.summary: Dataclass of what preparation did: identity pairs compared and index chunks refreshed.

nodes.name: prepare_changes
nodes.summary: Resolves identities and refreshes the retrieval index incrementally, the prerequisites every path from new entities to evaluation needs.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Runs ingest, normalization, preparation, evaluation enqueue and drain, and the state writer for a tenant, each step traced, and returns the RunReport.

nodes.name: format_report
nodes.summary: Formats a RunReport as readable lines.

nodes.name: writer.py
nodes.summary: State writer consuming the verdicts topic in order, writing exactly one bitemporal compliance_state row per verdict with its reason (human override, correction, rule change, stale evidence, late event, new evidence) and noting rule-change amendments.

nodes.name: WriteSummary
nodes.summary: Dataclass counting verdicts consumed, rows written, ones already written, missing verdicts, and rows by reason.

nodes.name: reason_for
nodes.summary: Chooses the compliance_state reason for a verdict from its trigger, rule stamp and timing relative to the head row.

nodes.name: already_written
nodes.summary: Whether a state row exists for a verdict id.

nodes.name: write_verdict
nodes.summary: Writes one state row for one verdict through the bitemporal writer, at the right valid time and reason, noting a rule-change amendment; returns None when it was written before.

nodes.name: StateWriterConsumer
nodes.summary: OrderedConsumer on the verdicts topic that loads each verdict and writes its state row in a traced step, tallying a WriteSummary.

nodes.name: drain
nodes.summary: Runs the state writer consumer once over everything waiting and returns its summary.

nodes.name: labels.py
nodes.summary: Turns consented reviewer decisions on tier 3 draft verdicts into labelled-set eval cases and exports them as YAML outside the repository, skipping regathers and other approval kinds.

nodes.name: InsideRepository
nodes.summary: Raised when the output path is inside the repository: reviewer labels hold customer data and never go there.

nodes.name: intake
nodes.summary: Builds labelled-set cases from review-label rows (approve means right, override or reject means wrong) and counts what was skipped and why.

nodes.name: outside_repository
nodes.summary: Checks that an output path resolves outside the repository root.

nodes.name: export
nodes.summary: Writes the tenant's consented reviewer labels as YAML to a path outside the repository and returns the count and the skips.

nodes.name: relabel.py
nodes.summary: Stratified nightly judge samples and the monthly expert relabel: stratifies verdicts by status, confidence band and evidence type, picks last month's batch for experts, records their labels, and checks expert-judge agreement against the calibrated interval.

nodes.name: Candidate
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass for a verdict that may be sampled: id, test, status, confidence and evidence type.

nodes.name: band
nodes.summary: Classifies a confidence as near, high, low or unknown relative to the review threshold.

nodes.name: weight
nodes.summary: Draw weight of a stratum: doubled for PASS results and for near-threshold ones, so both count four times.

nodes.name: stratify
nodes.summary: Draws at most `size` (stratum, candidate) pairs round by round with a seeded shuffle, giving every stratum one draw and risky strata extra.

nodes.name: record_judged
nodes.summary: Records one judged item with its stratum, status, confidence, the judge's call and model.

nodes.name: previous_month
nodes.summary: The YYYY-MM label of the month before a moment.

nodes.name: monthly_batch
nodes.summary: On the 1st, picks last month's relabel batch once: items the judge disagreed with first, then a spread over the strata.

nodes.name: batch
nodes.summary: The month's relabel items with their verdicts, the judge's call and any expert label.

nodes.name: label
nodes.summary: Records an expert's pass or fail label on a judged item.

nodes.name: latest_calibration
nodes.summary: Reads the overall row of the newest judge calibration report: agreement and its interval.

nodes.name: check
nodes.summary: Compares the month's expert-judge agreement against the calibrated interval and records it as a quality check that fails, asking for re-calibration, when it falls outside.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package docstring for the evaluators layer: the trigger, the three evaluation tiers, and verdicts.

nodes.name: inventory.py
nodes.summary: Records, per full run, the subjects each test is expected to have verdicts for and which listing scopes were not seen whole and fresh, and reads the newest inventories plus parked subjects as Coverage for the rollup.

nodes.name: gaps
nodes.summary: The listing scopes of the test in the context that were not seen whole and fresh.

nodes.name: record
nodes.summary: Appends this run's inventory of expected subjects and gaps for the test in the context.

nodes.name: coverage
nodes.summary: Reads the newest inventory of every test and the parked subject keys into a Coverage for the rollup.

nodes.name: rollup.py
nodes.summary: The requirement-state rule: a requirement takes the worst state among its linked tests' subjects (fail > needs_review > pending > partial > pass), counts unassessed, parked or stale subjects as pending, names the blocking test and subject, and notes exceptions without hiding failures.

nodes.name: Inventory
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass of a test's expected subjects as its newest full run listed them, with completeness, timing and gaps.

nodes.name: Coverage
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass of what the rollup needs besides the heads to tell a pass from an unknown: inventories, parked subjects and now.

nodes.name: RequirementRollup
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass of one requirement's rolled-up state: blocking test and subject, verdict ids, counts, per-test states, pending reasons and exception end.

nodes.name: FrameworkRollup
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass of a framework's requirement rollups, with whether no evaluations exist yet and a status summary.

nodes.name: _seen
nodes.summary: Lists what the rollup counts for one test: each expected or verdicted subject's state, pending when unassessed, parked or stale, or the test's own gap.

nodes.name: test_states
nodes.summary: A test's subjects as the rollup counts them, shared with audit preparation so a task and the rollup never disagree.

nodes.name: rollup
nodes.summary: Computes every requirement's worst state over its linked tests by precedence, naming the blocker and pending reasons; a requirement whose failing subjects are all excepted still fails and says until when.

nodes.name: format_rollup
nodes.summary: Formats a FrameworkRollup as readable lines with counts and pending reasons.

nodes.name: send.py
nodes.summary: Questionnaire staleness sweep, person-initiated sending that is refused until every answer is approved and current and records what left as an attestation and a file, and the metrics LT3 is judged by.

nodes.name: sweep
nodes.summary: Marks every approved answer stale whose verdicts no longer hold or whose cited documents have a newer version; registered as the daily answer_staleness job.

nodes.name: send
nodes.summary: Records that a person sent the questionnaire once every answer is approved and current, attesting the assertion under the publication policy and writing the record of what was sent.

nodes.name: Metrics
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass of questionnaire metrics: edit rate by question kind, stale, contradicted and failed-check counts.

nodes.name: metrics
nodes.summary: Computes reviewer edit rates per question kind, stale answers, answers contradicted by verdicts, and drafts that failed a code check.

nodes.name: store.py
nodes.summary: Persistence layer for security questionnaires: stores questionnaires and their drafted answers, records approve/reject events, keeps the approved-answer library, and computes why a reused answer has gone stale (A-163, A-164).
nodes.languageNotes: Answers are append-only: status changes are answer_events rows and the answer_status view lays the latest one over each answer.

nodes.name: question_key
nodes.summary: Normalizes question text to lowercase word tokens and SHA-256 hashes them so differently spaced or punctuated copies of a question share one key.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Inserts a questionnaire with its question list after checking every question has its own unique id; returns the new ULID.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Loads one questionnaire by id as a dict with parsed questions, status and send metadata.

nodes.name: Answer
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass for a drafted questionnaire answer (text, stages, checks, pointers, verdict ids, cost, status); exposes checks_passed and final_text (the person's edit, else the draft).

nodes.name: record_answer
nodes.summary: Persists a drafted answer from the pipeline or library with its question key, checks, pointers and verdict ids, then records a draft event.

nodes.name: event
nodes.summary: Appends an answer_events row (draft, approved, rejected) with actor, note and optional edited text.

nodes.name: answer
nodes.summary: Loads one answer by id from the answer_status view.

nodes.name: answers_of
nodes.summary: Returns the newest answer to each question of a questionnaire using DISTINCT ON over the answer_status view.

nodes.name: approve
nodes.summary: Approves an answer, edited or not; a draft that failed a code check is approved only with the person's own text, and the approved answer joins the reusable library.

nodes.name: reject
nodes.summary: Rejects a drafted answer with a mandatory note and records the rejection event.

nodes.name: stale_reasons
nodes.summary: Explains what changed since an answer was drafted: a relied-on verdict is no longer the subject's current state, or a cited document has a newer version.

nodes.name: LibraryEntry
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass for an approved answer in the reusable library: question key, text, pointers, verdict ids, source answer and approver.

nodes.name: match
nodes.summary: Finds a still-true approved library answer for a question: exact key first, else the closest by shared words (at least 80%); stale matches are skipped and their reasons returned.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the remediation layer (spec Layer 10) whose docstring lays out the design: a closed action catalogue, validated targets, approval-gated proposals, dry-run by default, five live gates, rollback and re-evaluation.

nodes.name: broker.py
nodes.summary: Credential broker for the remediation executor: issues a write credential bound to one approved operation only after re-checking the approval item and grant itself, and records every issue in the insert-only credential_issues table (A-116).

nodes.name: NotApproved
nodes.summary: Exception raised when no approved item stands behind an operation, so no credential is issued.

nodes.name: Credential
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass holding a write token (hidden from repr) bound to one operation, action and scope, with issue and expiry times.

nodes.name: issue
nodes.summary: Issues and records a credential for one approved operation after verifying the approval is decided, approved, its own and that any named grant was minted by it; returns None when no token is configured.

nodes.name: cli.py
nodes.summary: Typer command group for `ccp remediate`: propose, list, show, execute (dry run by default), rollback behind its own approval, and audit of actions without matching approvals; deliberately exposes no simulate command.

nodes.name: propose
nodes.summary: CLI command creating rule-fallback remediation proposals for one verdict; each waits in the approval stage.

nodes.name: list_cmd
nodes.summary: CLI command listing a tenant's remediation proposals as JSON.

nodes.name: show
nodes.summary: CLI command showing one proposal with the runner's description of its call, grant and journal.

nodes.name: execute
nodes.summary: CLI command executing a proposal, dry run by default; live requires all five gates, the decision's unspent grant and unchanged preconditions.

nodes.name: rollback
nodes.summary: CLI command creating or running a rollback proposal that restores the recorded pre-state behind its own approval and typed restore confirmation.

nodes.name: audit
nodes.summary: CLI command listing proposals that acted without a matching approval and exiting 1 if any exist.

nodes.name: gates.py
nodes.summary: Implements the five live-mode remediation gates (env flag, --live flag, allowed repo and unprotected login, exact typed confirmation phrase, and an approval by a named reviewer bound to the proposal's payload hash) that must all hold before any live call.

nodes.name: RemediationConfig
nodes.summary: Pydantic model (extra fields forbidden) listing the allowed org/repo targets and protected logins that gate 3 checks.

nodes.name: load_config
nodes.summary: Loads and validates the remediation config YAML, defaulting to an empty allow-list when the file is absent.

nodes.name: approval_matches
nodes.summary: Gate 5 check: the approval is approved, by a named reviewer, for exactly this payload hash.

nodes.name: GateCheck
nodes.summary: Result of evaluating the five gates: the list of missing gates, with passed and describe helpers.

nodes.name: check
nodes.summary: Evaluates all five live-mode gates for a proposal (env flag, --live, allowed repo/unprotected login, exact confirmation phrase, bound approval) and returns which are missing.

nodes.name: github_admin.py
nodes.summary: The only GitHub write surface in CCP: plans exact collaborator/org-member REST calls and defines a GitHubAdmin protocol with a live httpx implementation and a recording test double; never deletes repos, branches, files or orgs.
nodes.languageNotes: GitHubAdmin is a typing.Protocol, so LiveGitHubAdmin and RecordingGitHubAdmin satisfy it structurally without inheritance.

nodes.name: PlannedCall
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass describing an exact GitHub REST call (method, path, body) for dry runs and journaling.

nodes.name: GitHubAdmin
nodes.summary: Protocol for the three GitHub admin operations CCP may perform: read collaborator permission, remove a collaborator, add a collaborator.

nodes.name: LiveGitHubAdmin
nodes.summary: httpx-based GitHubAdmin implementation calling the GitHub REST API with a bearer token for permission reads and collaborator add/remove.

nodes.name: RecordingGitHubAdmin
nodes.summary: Test double implementing GitHubAdmin that records every call and simulates permissions in memory without contacting GitHub.

nodes.name: journal.py
nodes.summary: Append-only execution journal (A-131) recording what the remediation executor did with each grant: started, observed pre-state, finished or failed, keyed by proposal id plus payload hash so interrupted operations are detectable as in-doubt.

nodes.name: Entry
nodes.summary: Dataclass for one execution-journal row: operation, proposal, grant, entry kind, mode, detail and timestamp.

nodes.name: append
nodes.summary: Inserts one journal entry (started, observed, finished, failed) inside the caller's transaction.

nodes.name: entries
nodes.summary: Reads a proposal's journal entries in recorded order.

nodes.name: in_doubt
nodes.summary: Returns started journal entries with no finished or failed counterpart, meaning the executor stopped part-way.

nodes.name: preconditions.py
nodes.summary: Computes the code-derived preconditions a remediation proposal was made under (newest verdict status, the login's current access, or a reversed proposal's pre-state), hashes them, and diffs them so the executor refuses when the situation changed after approval.

nodes.name: Reversed
nodes.summary: Protocol describing the reversed proposal a rollback precondition reads: its id, status and recorded pre-state.

nodes.name: _access
nodes.summary: Looks up the login's current grant on one repository or organization from normalized persons, assets and grants.

nodes.name: current
nodes.summary: Computes the facts a proposal depends on now: the subject's newest verdict status, the login's access on the target, or for a rollback the reversed proposal's status and pre-state.

nodes.name: differences
nodes.summary: Describes in words which precondition fields changed, for the executor's refusal message.

nodes.name: proposals.py
nodes.summary: Store for remediation proposals and their approval items: creates immutable proposal rows with risk summary and precondition hash, opens the approval item, creates rollback reversals, and appends status changes as proposal_events.
nodes.languageNotes: Proposals are never updated; each status change is a new proposal_events row and the proposal_status view overlays the latest event.

nodes.name: Proposal
nodes.summary: Immutable remediation proposal record (action, target, risk, precondition, status fields) whose payload is what the approval shows and whose hash binds the approval to it.

nodes.name: payload_of
nodes.summary: Builds the approval payload from a proposal's action, target, rationale, risk summary and precondition hash.

nodes.name: _row
nodes.summary: Maps a proposal_status row into a Proposal, parsing JSON columns.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Inserts a proposal with its code-written risk summary and current precondition hash, then opens its remediation (or remediation_rollback) approval item.

nodes.name: create_reversal
nodes.summary: Creates a rollback proposal that undoes an original, restoring the permission recorded before it acted, waiting on its own approval.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Loads one proposal by id from the proposal_status view.

nodes.name: for_verdict
nodes.summary: Lists the proposals made for one verdict.

nodes.name: reversals
nodes.summary: Lists the rollback proposals made for a proposal, oldest first.

nodes.name: list_all
nodes.summary: Lists the tenant's proposals oldest first, optionally filtered by status.

nodes.name: record
nodes.summary: Appends one status change in its own transaction and returns the updated proposal.

nodes.name: record_in
nodes.summary: Appends one status change inside the caller's transaction, carrying unspecified fields over from the latest event.

nodes.name: _append
nodes.summary: Inserts a proposal_events row merging the given call, pre-state and refusal with the latest status.

nodes.name: reevaluate.py
nodes.summary: Closes the remediation loop by re-pulling the affected connector and pushing the new observations through the normal landing, normalization, impact, evaluation and state-writer pipeline rather than calling evaluators directly.

nodes.name: ReevaluationSummary
nodes.summary: Dataclass of counts from a re-evaluation pass: landed, normalized, enqueued, evaluated, state written and pull status.

nodes.name: reevaluate
nodes.summary: Re-pulls the affected connector and drains landing, normalization, impact, evaluations and the state writer so remediated findings are re-evaluated through the normal topic.

nodes.name: runner.py
nodes.summary: Core remediation orchestrator: proposes rule-fallback actions for a failing verdict, executes them as dry runs or live behind the five gates, an unspent grant and unchanged preconditions, simulates in fixture mode, rolls back via its own approved proposal, and audits actions lacking approvals.
nodes.languageNotes: Fail-closed design: a grant is consumed and the journal opened in one transaction before any external call, so a crash leaves an in-doubt entry instead of a silent retry.

nodes.name: ProposeSummary
nodes.summary: Dataclass collecting the proposals created and the targets rejected by one propose call.

nodes.name: propose
nodes.summary: Creates rule-fallback proposals for a verdict, validating each target against the tenant and the verdict's cited evidence; idempotent per verdict.

nodes.name: propose_for_verdict_id
nodes.summary: Loads a verdict by id and proposes remediations for it.

nodes.name: planned_call
nodes.summary: Maps a proposal's action to the exact GitHub call it would make, or None for log-only actions.

nodes.name: ExecutionResult
nodes.summary: Dataclass returned by execute/simulate/rollback: the updated proposal, mode and a human-readable message.

nodes.name: _cleared
nodes.summary: Checks the decision's grant is unspent and unexpired and the proposal's preconditions still hold; returns the grant or why not and whether a new decision is needed.

nodes.name: _refuse
nodes.summary: Records a refusal on the proposal, emits a step event, and optionally reopens an approval item to ask again.

nodes.name: execute
nodes.summary: Public entry for executing a proposal inside an observability step; dry run unless live is requested.

nodes.name: _execute
nodes.summary: The executor: plans the call, enforces the five gates, grant and preconditions, consumes the grant and opens the journal, obtains a broker credential, reads the pre-state, makes the single GitHub call, and journals the outcome.

nodes.name: _failed
nodes.summary: Marks an interrupted or failed call in the journal and on the proposal, keeps the grant spent, and opens a new approval item.

nodes.name: simulate
nodes.summary: Fixture-mode execution entry: applies gate 5, the grant and the precondition, then lets the test-only fixture hook apply the change.

nodes.name: _simulate
nodes.summary: Simulated executor: verifies the approval, grant and preconditions, consumes the grant and journals a simulated call without touching GitHub.

nodes.name: _reversal
nodes.summary: Returns the rollback proposal for a target, creating it if needed and closing open requests for other targets.

nodes.name: reversal_of
nodes.summary: Returns the newest rollback proposal made for a proposal.

nodes.name: rollback_requests
nodes.summary: Lists every approval item of every rollback proposal made for a proposal, oldest first.

nodes.name: rollback
nodes.summary: Rolls back an executed proposal as a proposal of its own: first call creates it with its approval item; once approved it runs through the same executor (simulated, dry-run, or live with a restore confirmation).

nodes.name: audit
nodes.summary: Finds actions without authorization: simulated, executed or rolled-back proposals lacking a finished journal record on a spent grant approved for their exact payload.

nodes.name: describe
nodes.summary: Builds a description of a proposal's planned call, approval, grant use and journal entries for display.

nodes.name: targets.py
nodes.summary: Compatibility shim that re-exports Resolution and resolve from ccp.evaluators.targets so the Layer 10 import path keeps working while the agent layer shares the target-validation implementation.

nodes.name: bitemporal.py
nodes.summary: Append-only bitemporal compliance-state table access (spec Layer 5): records verdict rows with valid time and transaction time, supersedes chain heads instead of updating, files late facts into history, and answers as-of, current and believed-state queries.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a per-tenant sequence row locked until commit to order transaction time, and contains no UPDATE statement by design.

nodes.name: StateRow
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass for one compliance_state row (subject, test, status, valid/recorded times, supersession, reason, history flag) with a from_row parser.

nodes.name: _next_seq
nodes.summary: Advances the tenant's transaction-time counter under a row lock held until commit.

nodes.name: record
nodes.summary: Appends a state row for a subject, superseding the chain head, or files a late fact into history bounded by the next newer fact.

nodes.name: state_as_of
nodes.summary: Returns what was true at a valid time according to everything recorded by a known time.

nodes.name: current_state
nodes.summary: Returns the latest belief about a valid time (default now).

nodes.name: chain
nodes.summary: Returns a subject's full supersession chain of state rows.

nodes.name: heads
nodes.summary: Returns every subject's current chain head (never history rows); the report reads these.

nodes.name: exceptions.py
nodes.summary: Stored control exceptions (A-132): a failing subject accepted until a date, minted only inside an approving decision's transaction, with time-aware reads that label a status as 'fail (excepted until D)' without ever turning it into a pass.

nodes.name: ControlException
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass for a stored control exception on a test and subject (reason, owner, valid-until, grantor, optional revocation) with holds(now) checking the grant window and revocation.

nodes.name: _row
nodes.summary: Maps a control_exceptions row into a ControlException.

nodes.name: insert
nodes.summary: Mints one control exception inside the approving decision's transaction.

nodes.name: revoke
nodes.summary: Marks a control exception revoked.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Loads one control exception by id.

nodes.name: active
nodes.summary: Maps subject keys to the exception holding at a moment, preferring the longer-lasting of two.

nodes.name: label
nodes.summary: Renders a status with its exception, e.g. 'fail (excepted until D)'; only failures are ever excepted.

nodes.name: scoped.py
nodes.summary: Defines ScopedDB, the only query surface for tenant data: every transaction sets app.tenant_id locally so Postgres row-level security filters every row, and no method accepts a tenant id argument.
nodes.languageNotes: set_config('app.tenant_id', ..., true) is transaction-local, so the tenant setting dies with the transaction and cannot leak across pooled connections.

nodes.name: ScopedDB
nodes.summary: Tenant-scoped database wrapper over a connection pool whose transaction() sets app.tenant_id for RLS, with fetch_all, fetch_one and execute helpers.

nodes.name: planners.py
nodes.summary: Code planners for agentic tasks (A-150): turn scoping facts and the control catalogue into check and read items for audit-prep and questionnaire tasks, settle checks from compliance-state heads, and add follow-up gap reads per control family.
nodes.languageNotes: Planner is a typing.Protocol; AuditPrep and Questionnaire are registered in a PLANNERS dict looked up by task kind.

nodes.name: Settlement
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass for what code concluded about a check item in one pass: final or open status, outcome, result and evidence ids.

nodes.name: Facts
nodes.summary: Per-pass snapshot of compliance-state heads grouped by test plus the rollup's coverage, read once and used to settle every check item.

nodes.name: Planner
nodes.summary: Protocol for task planners: plan items, count expected reads, settle checks, add follow-ups and recheck reads.

nodes.name: family_of
nodes.summary: Derives a requirement's control family from its id (CC6.1 -> CC6, A.5.15 -> A.5).

nodes.name: AuditPrep
nodes.summary: Audit-prep planner: one check item per in-scope test settled from rule verdicts, plus one model-filled gap read per control family whose checks settle with gaps.

nodes.name: Questionnaire
nodes.summary: Questionnaire planner: control-mapped questions become check items answered from verdicts; unmapped or undecided ones become read items.

nodes.name: planner_for
nodes.summary: Looks up the registered planner for a task kind, raising ValueError for unknown kinds.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for tenants-as-data (A-133) documenting its three modules: appended settings versions, onboarding without a deploy, and scope changes that need an approver.

nodes.name: onboarding.py
nodes.summary: Onboards a tenant without a deploy (A-133): validates the id, writes it into the tenant directory, records its first settings version from safe strict defaults, and makes the signer-up its first admin.

nodes.name: AlreadyExists
nodes.summary: Exception raised when onboarding a tenant id that already exists.

nodes.name: defaults
nodes.summary: Builds a new tenant's first settings with strict defaults where a status depends on them.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Creates a tenant: validates the id and uniqueness, inserts it into the tenant directory with its first settings version in one transaction, then grants the signer-up the admin role and evicts the cached tenant.

nodes.name: scope.py
nodes.summary: Handles changes to a tenant's settings (A-133): status-deciding or connection changes open a scope_change approval showing before/after and the tests affected, applied only if the base version is still current; other fields are recorded directly by an admin.

nodes.name: Superseded
nodes.summary: Exception raised when settings changed since a scope change was requested, so it must be asked again.

nodes.name: _affected
nodes.summary: Finds the tests a settings change reaches: rules naming the setting as a parameter, and for the GitHub org or connections, tests reading that connector.

nodes.name: change
nodes.summary: Requests a settings change: records non-scope fields directly as a version, or opens a scope_change approval item with before/after values and affected tests.

nodes.name: apply_in
nodes.summary: Applies an approved scope change as a new version inside the decision's transaction, refusing if the base version is no longer current.

nodes.name: versions.py
nodes.summary: Append-only versions of a tenant's settings (A-133): records new versions, reads current and history, and resolves the effective settings (latest stored version or the tenants file fallback).

nodes.name: Version
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass for one stored tenant-settings version: settings, status, reason, recorder, optional approval id and timestamp.

nodes.name: _row
nodes.summary: Maps a tenant_versions row into a Version with validated TenantSettings.

nodes.name: effective
nodes.summary: Returns the settings in force and their source: the latest stored version, else the tenants file.

nodes.name: record_in
nodes.summary: Appends a settings version inside the caller's transaction; the caller forgets the cached tenant after commit.

nodes.name: record
nodes.summary: Appends a settings version in its own transaction and evicts the cached tenant context.

nodes.name: test_remediation_loop.py
nodes.summary: End-to-end test of the simulated remediation loop: evaluates, finds Jane Smith's HR-1 failure, approves and simulates proposals, re-pulls through the fixture overlay, and asserts a pass row supersedes the fail; a rejected approval leaves state unchanged.

nodes.name: world
nodes.summary: Pytest fixture building a scratch database, running the full pipeline for the acme tenant with keyless providers, and yielding settings plus a ScopedDB; skips when Postgres is unreachable.

nodes.name: test_simulated_loop_closes_the_finding
nodes.summary: Approves and simulates Jane's remediation proposals, re-pulls via the fixture overlay, re-evaluates and asserts a pass row supersedes the fail with reason evaluation.

nodes.name: test_rejected_approval_leaves_state_unchanged
nodes.summary: Rejects a proposal's approval and asserts simulation is refused and compliance state stays unchanged.

nodes.name: test_bitemporal_props.py
nodes.summary: Hypothesis property test asserting that any sequence of bitemporal records never leaves a subject with two open rows and that every as-of query returns a row known at the time and covering the instant.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Hypothesis @given/@settings to generate record sequences against a real scratch database.

nodes.name: test_chain_invariants
nodes.summary: Hypothesis test recording random state sequences and checking each subject has at most one open head and as-of queries return known, covering rows.

nodes.name: test_action_targets.py
nodes.summary: Security test (S19 targets half) checking that remediation proposals name only this tenant's entities and the grant the verdict cited; off-tenant repos and uncited logins are dropped with guardrail events.

nodes.name: test_rule_fallback_proposes_the_tabled_actions_for_jane
nodes.summary: Checks rule fallback proposes exactly the tabled remediation actions for Jane Smith's HR-1 failure.

nodes.name: test_another_tenants_repo_is_rejected_with_a_guardrail_event
nodes.summary: Checks a target repo outside the tenant's org is rejected with a guardrail event.

nodes.name: test_a_login_the_verdict_never_cited_is_rejected
nodes.summary: Checks a login not cited by the verdict's evidence is rejected as a target.

nodes.name: test_approval_fail_closed.py
nodes.summary: Security test suite proving approvals fail closed (NT2, A-95): only well-formed named-reviewer decisions change drafts, tier 3 decisions survive failed resumes or commits, mismatched interrupts record nothing, rollbacks need their own bound approval, and audits find unapproved actions.
nodes.languageNotes: Mixes Hypothesis property tests with monkeypatched failure injection to exercise crash windows.

nodes.name: test_the_gate_changes_nothing_without_a_valid_decision
nodes.summary: Property test: apply_decision leaves a draft unchanged unless the decision is well-formed from a named reviewer.

nodes.name: test_build_refuses_ambiguous_decisions
nodes.summary: Checks decisions.build and validate refuse ambiguous combinations of action and edits.

nodes.name: world
nodes.summary: Fixture preparing tenants, refreshing the retrieval index and draining evaluations for tier 3 approval tests.

nodes.name: _interrupt
nodes.summary: Runs a tier 3 evaluation to its approval interrupt and returns the thread and approval item.

nodes.name: test_a_decision_is_recorded_first_and_survives_a_failed_resume
nodes.summary: Injects a resume failure and asserts the approval decision is recorded first and later applied once via resume.

nodes.name: test_a_failed_commit_after_the_resume_is_retried_from_the_final_state
nodes.summary: Injects a commit failure after resume and asserts a retry commits from the thread's final state.

nodes.name: test_an_item_that_does_not_show_the_pending_interrupt_records_nothing
nodes.summary: Checks an approval item whose payload is not the pending interrupt is refused with nothing recorded.

nodes.name: test_a_stored_decision_without_a_reviewer_is_held_for_review
nodes.summary: Checks a stored decision lacking a reviewer resumes the graph into needs_review.

nodes.name: test_resume_needs_this_threads_recorded_decision
nodes.summary: Checks tier 3 resume refuses a decision not recorded for this thread.

nodes.name: test_a_rollback_needs_its_own_approval_bound_to_what_it_restores
nodes.summary: Walks a rollback through creation, approval, execution and audit to prove it needs its own approval bound to the restored permission.

nodes.name: test_the_audits_find_actions_without_approvals
nodes.summary: Forges unapproved actions and decisions and asserts both the remediation and decisions audits report them.

nodes.name: test_copilot_cannot_act.py
nodes.summary: Security test (S11, S19) showing the copilot's 'fix this' never executes: it refuses the write tool, opens approvals only after an explicit yes, caps actions at two per turn, and rejects actions on another tenant's repo.

nodes.name: test_fix_this_refuses_the_write_tool_and_opens_an_approval_only_after_yes
nodes.summary: Asks the copilot to fix a finding and asserts it opens approval items only after an explicit yes and executes nothing.

nodes.name: test_three_requested_actions_yield_two_approvals_and_a_note
nodes.summary: Checks a turn requesting three actions opens at most two approvals and notes the rest.

nodes.name: test_an_action_on_another_tenants_repo_is_rejected_and_opens_nothing
nodes.summary: Checks a copilot action targeting another tenant's repo is rejected and opens no approval.

nodes.name: test_credentials.py
nodes.summary: Security test (MT3, A-116) asserting via AST scans that only ccp/credentials.py reads secrets and only the broker reaches the write credential, and that the broker issues credentials only for approved operations and the executor uses only those.

nodes.name: _calls_named
nodes.summary: AST-walks every ccp module to find call sites of a given function name, for static credential-access checks.

nodes.name: _fresh
nodes.summary: Creates a fresh remediation proposal for the acme verdict under test.

nodes.name: test_the_broker_issues_only_for_an_approved_operation_and_records_it
nodes.summary: Checks the broker refuses unapproved or mismatched operations and records each credential it issues without leaking the token.

nodes.name: test_the_executor_acts_only_with_the_brokers_credential
nodes.summary: Checks the live executor uses only the broker-issued credential for its GitHub client.

nodes.name: test_remediation_gates.py
nodes.summary: Security test (S8) parametrized over all 31 incomplete gate combinations proving remediation never calls GitHub without all five gates, makes exactly one call when all hold, rejects edited proposals by payload hash, and never removes org members live.

nodes.name: _fresh_proposal
nodes.summary: Clones the verdict's repo proposal so each gate combination starts from an un-refused proposal.

nodes.name: test_any_missing_gate_refuses_and_never_calls_github
nodes.summary: Parametrized over 31 gate combinations: any missing gate refuses, records the refusal, and never calls GitHub's delete.

nodes.name: test_all_five_gates_make_exactly_one_call_and_record_the_pre_state
nodes.summary: With all five gates, asserts exactly one GitHub call, a recorded pre-state, a clean audit and a working rollback.

nodes.name: test_an_edited_proposal_fails_the_payload_hash_check
nodes.summary: Edits a proposal behind the application's back as the DB owner and asserts the payload-hash gate refuses it.

nodes.name: test_org_member_removal_is_never_live
nodes.summary: Asserts org-member removal proposals are refused as not live-capable even with every gate satisfied.

nodes.name: test_chaos_workers.py
nodes.summary: Chaos workflow test (MT2, A-111) running evaluation workers and a state writer as separate processes, overlapping a deploy and hard-killing workers mid-step, then asserting nothing is lost, duplicated or dead-lettered and tenant caps hold.

nodes.name: _Fleet
nodes.summary: Test helper that starts, kills and stops worker subprocesses (evaluation consumers and state writer) with per-process logs.

nodes.name: test_workers_killed_mid_step_during_a_deploy_lose_and_duplicate_nothing
nodes.summary: Runs two overlapping worker fleets, hard-kills the first mid-step, and asserts exactly-once records, one verdict per key, one state row per verdict, and respected caps.

nodes.name: test_compliance_state.py
nodes.summary: Layer 9 workflow test: `ccp run` populates compliance state, Jane Smith's HR-1 row fails, the writer is idempotent, trigger reasons map onto supersession reasons, the chain answers both audit questions, and state is tenant-scoped.

nodes.name: world
nodes.summary: Fixture building a scratch database, running the pipeline for the acme and globex tenants, and yielding settings, per-tenant ScopedDBs and the acme run report; skips when Postgres is unreachable.

nodes.name: test_run_populates_state_and_jane_hr1_is_fail
nodes.summary: Checks a run populates compliance state with Jane Smith's HR-1 row failing and a readable report.

nodes.name: test_rollup_names_the_blocking_subject
nodes.summary: Checks the framework rollup names the blocking subject for CC6.2.

nodes.name: _verdict
nodes.summary: Builds a synthetic Verdict with a rule stamp and evaluation key for supersession tests.

nodes.name: test_trigger_reasons_map_onto_supersession_reasons_and_the_chain_answers_both_questions
nodes.summary: Commits verdicts with different triggers and asserts supersession reasons and that the chain answers both as-of and believed-state audit questions.

nodes.name: test_state_is_tenant_scoped_and_globex_has_its_own_heads
nodes.summary: Checks compliance state is tenant-scoped and the globex tenant has its own heads and counts.

nodes.name: cells.py
nodes.summary: Loads the deployment cells from config/cells.yaml and resolves the cell this process serves; a cell fixes the tenant's region, data residency and how models are reached (first-party API or regional Bedrock profiles), and wraps the SDK client so pinned model ids map to the cell's provider ids.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a frozen dataclass plus functools.lru_cache for a memoized YAML loader, and a thin proxy (ModelRouted/_Messages) that rewrites the `model` kwarg before delegating to the SDK.

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: The only module that reads the environment: a pydantic-settings Settings object covering storage, queue, auth, raw zone, AWS, models and eval paths, plus per-tenant configuration (schedules, connections, budgets) validated from config/tenants.yaml.
nodes.languageNotes: pydantic-settings maps field names to environment variables case-insensitively; secrets are typed SecretStr and frozen BaseModels with extra='forbid' reject unknown tenant keys.

nodes.name: credentials.py
nodes.summary: The single place a secret is read: maps each declared credential purpose (model, judge, embeddings, rerank, tracing, GitHub, OIDC, IdP, HRIS) to its Settings field and exposes the GitHub write token only to the remediation broker.
nodes.languageNotes: A typing.Literal 'Purpose' alias makes every secret read name a purpose that a type checker can verify.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the evaluation harness (spec Layer 11); holds only a docstring and no code.

nodes.name: adversarial.py
nodes.summary: The prompt-injection (S17) eval suite: loads adversarial cases as golden cases on the adversarial_tier2 target and poisons a scratch database by inserting a payload chunk beside a subject's real evidence chunk so tier 2 can be compared against its unpoisoned control.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Parses config/cells.yaml into a memoized mapping of cell id to Cell.

nodes.name: current
nodes.summary: Returns the Cell named by Settings.ccp_cell, raising when it is not defined in cells.yaml.

nodes.name: Cell
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass describing one deployment cell (region, residency, provider, model region, Bedrock profiles, Voyage URL); model_id maps a pinned model id to the provider id and refuses models without a regional profile.

nodes.name: ModelRouted
nodes.summary: Proxy around an SDK client whose messages API maps every model argument to the cell's provider-specific id.

nodes.name: _Messages
nodes.summary: Wraps the SDK messages resource so create, parse and stream calls have their model kwarg rewritten through the cell's model_id mapping.

nodes.name: ScheduleSpec
nodes.summary: Validated spec of one scheduled tenant job: job kind, an 'every N minutes/hours' or 'daily HH:MM' cadence, and an optional IANA time zone.

nodes.name: ConnectionSpec
nodes.summary: Validated spec of one tenant connection: connector type, fixture or live source, provider account, and the credential purpose it uses (never a secret).

nodes.name: TenantSettings
nodes.summary: Per-tenant configuration from tenants.yaml: org, admin limits, critical tags, SLA, daily budget, concurrency, label consent, time zone, cell, schedules and connections, with validators for zones, unique schedule ids and one connection per source.

nodes.name: TenantsFile
nodes.summary: Top-level schema of config/tenants.yaml mapping tenant ids to TenantSettings.

nodes.name: Settings
nodes.summary: All runtime configuration loaded from environment variables: database URLs and pooling, cell, data paths, raw store, AWS, audit, queue leases and retries, auth/OIDC, secrets, model ids and eval paths, with derived model and directory properties and a tenants-file loader.

nodes.name: secret
nodes.summary: Returns the secret value for one declared purpose from Settings, or None when it is not configured.

nodes.name: configured
nodes.summary: Reports whether the setting behind a credential purpose is set, without reading the secret.

nodes.name: remediation_token
nodes.summary: Returns GitHub's write token, intended only for the remediation broker.

nodes.name: load_adversarial
nodes.summary: Loads evals/adversarial/cases.yaml and turns each injection case into a GoldenCase on the adversarial_tier2 target, validating attack class and placement.

nodes.name: apply_placement
nodes.summary: Places an injection payload into base text by prepending, appending, replacing or inserting it into a markdown table cell.

nodes.name: base_chunk
nodes.summary: Fetches the subject's first real (non-distractor) chunk of an evidence type so a poisoned chunk can copy its metadata.

nodes.name: poison
nodes.summary: Embeds payload text and inserts it as an extra chunk beside the base chunk in the tenant's scratch database, returning the new chunk id.

nodes.name: unpoison
nodes.summary: Deletes a poisoned chunk by id after an adversarial case runs.

nodes.name: poisoned_count
