nodes.summary: Returns a dead parallel record to pending with fresh attempts.

nodes.name: status_of
nodes.summary: Returns a record's current status and attempts.

nodes.name: db_now
nodes.summary: Returns the database's current timestamp.

nodes.name: OrderedFailure
nodes.summary: Frozen per-consumer failure state of an ordered-topic record (attempts, status, last error, next attempt).

nodes.name: ordered_failures
nodes.summary: Loads a consumer's failure rows for a set of ordered-topic offsets.

nodes.name: record_ordered_failure
nodes.summary: Counts a failed try for an ordered consumer, scheduling a backoff or marking it dead after max_attempts or a terminal error.

nodes.name: resolve_ordered_failure
nodes.summary: Marks a consumer's ordered failure for an offset as resolved.

nodes.name: dead_ordered
nodes.summary: Lists dead ordered-topic failures per consumer.

nodes.name: dead_parallel
nodes.summary: Lists dead records on parallel topics.

nodes.name: record_replay
nodes.summary: Writes an audit row to dead_letter_replays for a replay attempt with who ran it and the outcome.

nodes.name: DeadLetter
nodes.summary: Frozen view of one dead letter: offset, topic, consumer (None on parallel topics), attempts and error.

nodes.name: dead_letters
nodes.summary: Lists parallel and per-consumer ordered dead letters sorted by offset.

nodes.name: _ordered_consumer
nodes.summary: Finds the registered ordered consumer with a given name and topic in the worker registry.

nodes.name: replay
nodes.summary: Replays one dead record: requeues it on a parallel topic, or re-runs it through each ordered consumer that dead-lettered it, recording every replay.

nodes.name: unpark
nodes.summary: Moves a topic's parked records back to pending and wakes its workers.

nodes.name: next_slot
nodes.summary: Computes the first UTC moment after a time that an `every N minutes|hours` or DST-aware `daily HH:MM` schedule names.

nodes.name: Fired
nodes.summary: Frozen record of one fired schedule slot and how many missed slots were folded into it.

nodes.name: sync
nodes.summary: Brings the tenant's schedules table in line with configuration, giving new or changed schedules a next slot and disabling removed ones.

nodes.name: fire_due
nodes.summary: Fires every due schedule once in the transaction: records the slot run, appends a jobs-topic record, and advances next_run_at past now while counting folded slots.

nodes.name: Scheduler
nodes.summary: Worker-loop adapter registered as `scheduler` that syncs and fires a tenant's schedules each pass and reports the next due slot.

nodes.name: TopicKind
nodes.summary: StrEnum of topic kinds: ordered or parallel.

nodes.name: kind_of
nodes.summary: Looks up a topic's kind, raising ValueError for undeclared topics.

nodes.name: worker.py
nodes.summary: Worker loop (spec A-106): a consumer registry plus a Dispatcher that serves one named consumer across many tenants fairly via work hints, waking on Postgres LISTEN notifications, due hints, or periodic sweeps, and isolating per-tenant errors.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the Investigator (spec Layer 14), which finds root cause and missing evidence and proposes bounded fixes for failing verdicts without ever acting.

nodes.name: Runnable
nodes.summary: Protocol for anything the worker loop drives: a name, a topic and run_once returning work done.

nodes.name: register
nodes.summary: Decorator that registers a consumer or producer factory by name in the CONSUMERS registry.

nodes.name: RawAuditConsumer
nodes.summary: Phase-2 demonstration ordered consumer that logs each raw record as a traced step.

nodes.name: Dispatcher
nodes.summary: Serves one registered consumer across many tenants: sweeps and LISTENs for work hints, claims the longest-ago-served tenant, runs a quantum, and puts the hint back with its next due time while isolating per-tenant errors.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Builds a Dispatcher for a consumer and tenants, runs it once or continuously, and always closes it.

nodes.name: completeness.py
nodes.summary: Completeness guard (A-123) that withholds a tier-1 PASS or PARTIAL as needs_review when any source scope it rests on was not seen whole and fresh, and digests those scope states into the evaluation key so a population going partial or stale triggers a new evaluation.

nodes.name: context.py
nodes.summary: Defines the EvaluationContext every evaluator sees (tenant entities, identity links, pending reviews, test spec, trigger, clock, source states) and loads it as of a single observation watermark so evaluations can be re-derived later.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Tier-1 deterministic evaluator package entry that dispatches each test to its hand-coded rule module (GH-1/2/3/5, HR-1/5) or to a declarative YAML check loaded at import time; no model call is allowed anywhere in the package.

nodes.name: common.py
nodes.summary: Shared helpers for the deterministic rules: subject-key formatting, terminated HRIS person lookup, HR person resolution through identity groups, and newest-timestamp selection.

nodes.name: declarative.py
nodes.summary: Total interpreter for declarative tier-1 checks written as YAML (A-127): pydantic models validate a check's read, abstain, population and require clauses and its reasoning templates at load, and evaluate() applies them to the tenant's entities to produce a verdict.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses pydantic model_validator hooks and string.Formatter parsing to reject unknown entity fields and template placeholders at load time, keeping the YAML DSL total (no loops, expressions or code).

nodes.name: gh1.py
nodes.summary: GH-1 tier-1 rule: flags a person terminated in HRIS who still holds active GitHub org or repo access observed after the termination, deferring to needs_review on pending identity links or missing post-termination observations.

nodes.name: state_of
nodes.summary: Classifies one required source scope as complete, stale, never_pulled, or the status its latest pull left (partial, not_visible, failed).

nodes.name: digest
nodes.summary: Builds a sorted 'scope=state' string of a test's required sources so source completeness becomes part of the evaluation key.

nodes.name: gaps
nodes.summary: Lists (scope, reason) pairs for every required scope that is not complete and fresh, with human-readable explanations.

nodes.name: guard
nodes.summary: Downgrades a PASS or PARTIAL verdict to needs_review when required sources have gaps, keeping the rule's reasoning and adding incomplete_source guardrail events; a FAIL passes through unchanged.

nodes.name: EvaluationContext
nodes.summary: Dataclass bundling a tenant's current persons, grants, assets, evidence, canonical identity map and pending reviews for one evaluation; provides identity-group lookups, SLA and valid-from strategies, the input manifest, and a factory for deterministic tier-1 verdicts.

nodes.name: load_context
nodes.summary: Loads an EvaluationContext from the scoped DB as of the tenant's current observation watermark (or a recorded one for re-derivation), pulling entities, identity resolution state and latest source scopes.

nodes.name: subjects_for
nodes.summary: Returns the subjects a tier-1 test judges, using the declarative check when one exists for the test and otherwise the rule module's subjects().

nodes.name: evaluate
nodes.summary: Evaluates one subject of a tier-1 test by delegating to the declarative interpreter or the test's rule module and returning its Verdict.

nodes.name: subject_key
nodes.summary: Formats a verdict subject key as '<test_id>|<scope>'.

nodes.name: terminated_hr_persons
nodes.summary: Returns HRIS person records whose employment status is terminated, sorted by entity id.

nodes.name: hr_person_for
nodes.summary: Finds the HRIS person entity within a canonical identity group, or None when the group has none.

nodes.name: latest
nodes.summary: Returns the most recent of the given optional timestamps, or None when none is known.

nodes.name: Condition
nodes.summary: Pydantic model for one check condition: a dot-path field with exactly one test (equals, in, truthy, at_least, at_most, exists), validated at load and evaluated against an entity by holds().

nodes.name: Read
nodes.summary: Pydantic model for a check's read clause: the entity collection to read (persons, grants, assets or evidence) and its filter conditions.

nodes.name: Abstain
nodes.summary: Pydantic model for a check's abstain clause: the fixed needs_review reason and guardrail events used when nothing was read.

nodes.name: Population
nodes.summary: Pydantic model narrowing what a check read to the population it judges via extra conditions.

nodes.name: Check
nodes.summary: Top-level pydantic model for a declarative check that validates every condition field against the source entity model and limits fail and pass reasoning templates to allowed placeholders.

nodes.name: _field
nodes.summary: Resolves a dot path into an entity or nested dict, returning None on any missing step and an enum's value for enums.

nodes.name: file_stem
nodes.summary: Maps a test id to the file stem its check lives in (HR-2 -> hr2).

nodes.name: load_all
nodes.summary: Loads and validates every YAML check under knowledge/checks, enforcing that each file is named after its test and that no test has two checks.

nodes.name: subjects
nodes.summary: Returns the single 'tenant' subject that every declarative check judges.

nodes.name: evaluate
nodes.summary: Runs a declarative check: reads and filters the source collection, abstains when it is empty, narrows the population, and returns a FAIL naming failing entities or a PASS with formatted reasoning.

nodes.name: subjects
nodes.summary: Lists terminated HR persons as canonical 'person:' subjects for GH-1.

nodes.name: evaluate
nodes.summary: Decides GH-1 for one terminated person: needs_review without a termination record or with a pending identity link, FAIL when GitHub grants were seen active after termination, otherwise PASS or needs_review.

nodes.name: gh2.py
nodes.summary: GH-2 tier-1 rule: checks that each GitHub organization's active admin count stays within the tenant's configured limit.

nodes.name: gh3.py
nodes.summary: GH-3 tier-1 rule: checks that each repository's default branch requires at least one approving review before merge, returning PARTIAL when admins are exempt and needs_review when no protection snapshot exists.

nodes.name: gh5.py
nodes.summary: GH-5 tier-1 rule: scans every evidence row attached to a repository for plaintext secrets, failing on any hit and withholding a PASS when no file listing exists or not every listed file was read.

nodes.name: hr1.py
nodes.summary: HR-1 tier-1 rule and the core cross-system case: a terminated person must have zero active access grants across every connected system within the termination SLA, classifying each grant as fine, revoked late, violating or unknown.

nodes.name: hr5.py
nodes.summary: HR-5 tier-1 rule: every shared or generic account must have a documented individual owner who is an active employee, and an account registry must have been observed before any PASS.

nodes.name: rederive.py
nodes.summary: Re-derives a stored tier-1 verdict from its recorded input manifest (watermark, clock, source runs, parameters) and classifies the result as exact, rule_changed or mismatch; a nightly sentinel samples verdicts and logs each outcome to replay_checks.

nodes.name: subjects
nodes.summary: Lists every organization asset as an 'org:' subject for GH-2.

nodes.name: evaluate
nodes.summary: Counts active admin grants on an organization and returns FAIL when they exceed the tenant's configured admin limit, else PASS, naming the admins.

nodes.name: subjects
nodes.summary: Lists every repository asset as a sorted 'repo:' subject for GH-3.

nodes.name: evaluate
nodes.summary: Reads a repository's branch_protection settings and returns FAIL when unprotected or no approving review is required, PARTIAL when admins are exempt, PASS otherwise, or needs_review without a snapshot.

nodes.name: subjects
nodes.summary: Lists every repository asset as a sorted 'repo:' subject for GH-5.

nodes.name: evaluate
nodes.summary: Scans a repository's evidence text with the secret patterns and returns FAIL on hits, needs_review when no file listing exists or listed files went unread, else PASS.

nodes.name: subjects
nodes.summary: Lists terminated HR persons as canonical 'person:' subjects for HR-1.

nodes.name: evaluate
nodes.summary: Classifies every grant in the person's canonical group against the termination-plus-SLA deadline and returns FAIL on violations, needs_review on grants unobserved since, or PASS with late revocations recorded as guardrail events.

nodes.name: subjects
nodes.summary: Returns the single 'tenant' subject for HR-5.

nodes.name: evaluate
nodes.summary: Finds shared accounts whose owner is missing or not an active employee: needs_review without an account registry, FAIL naming unowned accounts, else PASS.

nodes.name: Rederivation
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass holding one re-derivation's verdict id, test, subject, outcome, field diffs and the derived verdict.

nodes.name: rederive
nodes.summary: Rebuilds the evaluation context at a verdict's recorded watermark, clock and source scopes, reruns the deterministic rule with recorded or current parameters, and diffs the compared fields into exact, rule_changed or mismatch.

nodes.name: record
nodes.summary: Appends a re-derivation outcome and its diff to the replay_checks table in a tenant-scoped transaction.

nodes.name: sentinel
nodes.summary: Nightly job that re-derives the newest tier-1 verdict of up to a sample of subjects and records each outcome.

nodes.name: registry.py
nodes.summary: Tier evaluator registry that lets higher layers such as the tier-3 agent register evaluators at import time, so the evaluations consumer can dispatch tiers without importing the agent package.

nodes.name: rule_changes.py
nodes.summary: Implements rule-change semantics (A-128): amendments recorded by default with a notice so the past stands, and explicit corrections that re-decide each subject's past under the current rule with a preview, a named sign-off for FAIL-to-PASS flips, and a rule_changes notice.

nodes.name: rule_versions.py
nodes.summary: Computes rule versions (A-101): a sha256 of each test's deciding source files plus a hash of its parameters and the tenant settings rules read, combined into the rule stamp stored on every verdict and folded into its evaluation key.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Registry of pure decision rules for the AI tiers (R5) mapping rule names to decide(fields, params, clock) functions over citation-verified field values, plus the Decision result type.

nodes.name: gh4.py
nodes.summary: GH-4 decision rule for vulnerability disclosure policies: PASS when a verified response timeline is stated, PARTIAL when a policy states none, FAIL when no policy exists, needs_review when a deciding field lost its citation.

nodes.name: hr3.py
nodes.summary: HR-3 decision rule for security training: PASS when the record names this employee, is completed and is within the evidence max age, PARTIAL when stale, FAIL when someone else's or incomplete, needs_review when fields are unknown.

nodes.name: register_tier
nodes.summary: Registers an evaluator callable for a tier number.

nodes.name: evaluator_for
nodes.summary: Returns the evaluator registered for a tier, or None so the consumer parks the record.

nodes.name: registered_tiers
nodes.summary: Lists the registered tier numbers in ascending order.

nodes.name: describe
nodes.summary: Maps each registered tier to the module of its evaluator for diagnostics.

nodes.name: Flip
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass of one subject's status before and after a rule change.

nodes.name: Preview
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass previewing a rule change for a test: the old and new stamps and per-subject flips, with fail_to_pass and changed helpers.

nodes.name: Corrected
nodes.summary: Result of a recorded correction: change id, the preview, the verdict ids written and the notice text.

nodes.name: SignOffRequired
nodes.summary: PermissionError raised when a correction would turn a FAIL into a PASS without a named sign-off.

nodes.name: current_stamp
nodes.summary: Returns the current rule stamp of a test under the tenant's settings.

nodes.name: _old_verdicts
nodes.summary: Selects, per subject, the newest compliance-state verdict recorded under a rule stamp other than the current one, skipping subjects a correction under it already superseded.

nodes.name: preview
nodes.summary: Shows each subject's last verdict under an old rule alongside what the current rule decides from the same recorded inputs.

nodes.name: _record
nodes.summary: Inserts a rule_changes row (amendment or correction) with stamps, decider, sign-off, subjects and notice, idempotent per tenant, test, stamp and kind.

nodes.name: note_amendment
nodes.summary: Appends the amendment notice once per test and new stamp when the state writer first records a subject re-decided under a new rule.

nodes.name: correct
nodes.summary: Re-decides a test's past under its current rule: requires a named decider, refuses FAIL-to-PASS flips without sign-off, commits the corrected verdicts and records the correction notice.

nodes.name: rule_files
nodes.summary: Locates the source files that decide a test: its declarative YAML check plus the interpreter, or its deterministic or AI-tier rule module plus the shared helpers.

nodes.name: rule_version
nodes.summary: Cached 12-character sha256 over a test's rule files with line endings normalized.

nodes.name: parameters_hash
nodes.summary: Hashes a test's parameters, evidence max age, required sources and the rule-relevant tenant settings as canonical JSON.

nodes.name: rule_stamp
nodes.summary: Combines the rule version and parameters hash into the '<version>:<parameters>' stamp.

nodes.name: Decision
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass of a rule's decided VerdictStatus and its reasons.

nodes.name: decide
nodes.summary: Looks up a named AI-tier rule and applies it to verified fields, parameters and the clock, raising a descriptive KeyError for unknown rules.

nodes.name: decide
nodes.summary: Decides GH-4 from verified fields policy_exists, timeline_stated and timeline_text, returning needs_review whenever a deciding field is unknown or unverified.

nodes.name: parse_date
nodes.summary: Parses the first ten characters of a value as an ISO date, returning None for missing or invalid input.

nodes.name: decide
nodes.summary: Decides HR-3 from whether the record names the employee, its completion status and its completion date relative to the evidence max age.

nodes.name: hr4.py
nodes.summary: HR-4 decision rule for access reviews: compares the critical systems inventory with the latest review's scope by normalized name, yielding PASS, PARTIAL naming missing systems, FAIL, or needs_review when a list is unknown.

nodes.name: runner.py
nodes.summary: The evaluations consumer and full-run enqueuer (Layer 7): routes each evaluation record by tier, reuses already-stored verdicts, applies the daily model budget to AI tiers, the completeness guard and the second reader, then commits the verdict and its announcement atomically.

nodes.name: targets.py
nodes.summary: Validates remediation proposal targets (R12, S19): a target login, repo or org must resolve to this tenant's entities and the affected grant must be cited by the originating verdict, otherwise it is rejected with a guardrail event.

nodes.name: verdict.py
nodes.summary: Shared Verdict and Citation schema for every evaluator tier plus its persistence: an evaluation-key hash that makes retries no-ops, an idempotent insert stamped with the release bundle, and loaders by id, key, subject and test.

nodes.name: normalize_name
nodes.summary: Lowercases a system name and strips non-alphanumeric characters for matching.

nodes.name: compare
nodes.summary: Splits critical systems into missing and covered lists against the review's in-scope systems, preserving inventory order.

nodes.name: decide
nodes.summary: Decides HR-4 by comparing critical systems with the latest access review's scope, naming missing systems and the review date in its reasons.

nodes.name: cached_graph
nodes.summary: Process-wide cached load of the knowledge graph of frameworks, controls and tests.

nodes.name: RunSummary
nodes.summary: Dataclass counting enqueued, evaluated and duplicate evaluations and verdicts by status.

nodes.name: evaluate_request
nodes.summary: Evaluates one (test, subject) request: tier 1 through the deterministic rules and completeness guard, tiers 2 and 3 through the registered evaluator and second reader, parking when an AI tier is unavailable and counting model refusals.

nodes.name: commit_verdict
nodes.summary: Inserts a verdict and appends its announcement on the verdicts topic in one transaction, returning False when the evaluation key already existed.

nodes.name: cached_tenant_settings
nodes.summary: Returns the tenant's current settings version, falling back to the tenants file, via tenancy lookup.

nodes.name: expected_key
nodes.summary: Computes the evaluation key a routed tier will use before it runs, from model, prompt version, rule stamp and, for tier 1, the required sources' states.

nodes.name: unannounced
nodes.summary: Counts stored verdicts with no announcement on the verdicts topic, a reconciler check expected to be zero.

nodes.name: EvaluationsConsumer
nodes.summary: ParallelConsumer on the evaluations topic (one record in flight per subject, capped by tenant max_concurrency) that reuses stored verdicts by key, enforces the daily budget for AI tiers, evaluates, commits and tallies a RunSummary inside an observability step.

nodes.name: enqueue_all
nodes.summary: Enqueues every (test, subject) pair for the selected tests and tiers with the newest observation as trigger, recording each test's expected population inventory.

nodes.name: drain
nodes.summary: Runs an EvaluationsConsumer until no records remain and returns its summary.

nodes.name: requeue_parked
nodes.summary: Moves parked records on a topic back to pending and notifies listeners.

nodes.name: parked_count
nodes.summary: Counts parked records on a topic.

nodes.name: Resolution
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass of a target resolution: ok flag, reason, resolved grant ids and guardrail events.

nodes.name: resolve
nodes.summary: Resolves a proposal action's target to cited, active GitHub grants of this tenant for repo-collaborator or org-member removal, passing notify and request-evidence actions and rejecting unknown logins, repos, orgs, actions or uncited grants.

nodes.name: Citation
nodes.summary: Frozen pydantic model of a cited evidence chunk: chunk id, quote of at most 300 characters, what it supports and whether it was verified.

nodes.name: Verdict
nodes.summary: Frozen pydantic model shared by every tier carrying status, reasoning, citations, evidence refs, confidence, model and prompt metadata, trigger and valid time, rule version, input manifest and release bundle.

nodes.name: evaluation_key
nodes.summary: SHA-256 over tenant, test, subject, trigger time, prompt version, model, rule stamp and optional source states, used as the UNIQUE idempotency key.

nodes.name: persist
nodes.summary: Insert-or-ignore of a verdict in its own transaction, returning False when it already existed.

nodes.name: insert
nodes.summary: Inserts a verdict inside the caller's transaction with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on the evaluation key, stamping and registering the release bundle.

nodes.name: _from_row
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a Verdict from a verdicts table row, decoding its JSON columns.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Loads one verdict by id.

nodes.name: load_by_key
nodes.summary: Loads the stored verdict for an evaluation key, checked before any model call.

nodes.name: latest_per_subject
nodes.summary: Returns the newest verdict for every subject key, optionally restricted to one test.

nodes.name: latest_for_subject
nodes.summary: Returns the newest verdict for one subject key, what CCP believes now.

nodes.name: all_for_test
nodes.summary: Returns every verdict of a test in creation order.

nodes.name: count
nodes.summary: Counts the verdicts visible to the tenant.

nodes.name: blocking.py
nodes.summary: Blocking stage of identity resolution: derives cheap normalized keys (email, local part, employee id, initial-plus-surname, handles) and generates candidate person pairs that share a key across different connectors within one tenant, recording which keys matched.

nodes.name: normalize_email
nodes.summary: Lowercases an email and strips dots and any +suffix from the local part so equivalent addresses compare equal.

nodes.name: local_part
nodes.summary: Returns the normalized local part of an email address.

nodes.name: fold
nodes.summary: ASCII-folds text by NFKD-decomposing it and dropping combining marks, for accent-insensitive name comparison.

nodes.name: name_key
nodes.summary: Builds a first-initial-plus-surname key from a display name, or None when it has fewer than two tokens.

nodes.name: block_keys
nodes.summary: Computes the set of prefixed blocking keys (email, local, employee, name, handle) for one Person.

nodes.name: CandidatePair
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass pairing two Person records with the sorted block keys that caused them to be compared.

nodes.name: candidate_pairs
nodes.summary: Indexes persons by block key and emits deterministic, sorted pairs drawn from different source connectors of the same tenant, each carrying the keys that matched.

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: Frozen pydantic models for identity-resolution feature weights and routing thresholds, loaded and validated from config/identity.yaml and recorded on every resolution decision.

nodes.name: Weights
nodes.summary: Frozen model of per-feature scoring weights: exact email, local-part/handle matches, surname and initial, strong and weak Jaro-Winkler name similarity, employee id equality and a conflicting-emails penalty.

nodes.name: Thresholds
nodes.summary: Frozen model of the auto_merge and auto_distinct score cutoffs that route candidate pairs.

nodes.name: IdentityConfig
nodes.summary: Root identity-resolution configuration combining weights and thresholds, with a load classmethod that validates config/identity.yaml (or a given path).

nodes.name: resolver.py
nodes.summary: Identity resolver for a tenant: turns candidate pairs into logged decisions, writes person links on auto-merge, queues review items through the approval service, skips pairs whose features are unchanged, and offers watermark-aware reads of canonical links and pending reviews.
nodes.languageNotes: resolution_writer returns a closure so a reviewer's resolution is written inside the deciding approval event's transaction.

nodes.name: ResolutionSummary
nodes.summary: Mutable tally for one resolution run: pairs compared, unchanged pairs skipped and a count per route.

nodes.name: _pair_fingerprints
nodes.summary: Loads each decided pair's latest gate result and features as canonical JSON fingerprints so re-runs can skip unchanged pairs.

nodes.name: record_decision
nodes.summary: Persists one resolution decision with its block keys, features, score and thresholds; on auto_merge links both persons to a chosen canonical id and announces the change, on review enqueues the pair and opens an identity_merge approval item.

nodes.name: review_payload
nodes.summary: Builds the reviewer-facing payload: both person cards, the score and features, and what approving or rejecting means.

nodes.name: _announce_link
nodes.summary: Appends an entities-topic event for a person whose link changed so the impact step re-evaluates that person's tests.

nodes.name: resolve_tenant
nodes.summary: Runs identity resolution for one tenant: loads current persons, generates and scores candidate pairs, skips unchanged fingerprints, records decisions and reports route counts inside an observability step.

nodes.name: canonical_map
nodes.summary: Returns the person-to-canonical-id mapping for every linked person, optionally as of an observation watermark.

nodes.name: canonical_id
nodes.summary: Resolves an entity id to its canonical person id, falling back to the id itself when unlinked.

nodes.name: pending_review_entities
nodes.summary: Returns the entity ids involved in open identity reviews, optionally as of a watermark, so tests involving them report needs_review.

nodes.name: ReviewItem
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass for one open identity review: decision id, both entity ids, score, features and when it opened.

nodes.name: open_reviews
nodes.summary: Lists open identity review items joined with their decisions, oldest first.

nodes.name: resolution_writer
nodes.summary: Validates a reviewer's merge or distinct outcome for an open review and returns a writer that records the resolution, links both records on merge, and announces the affected persons inside the approval transaction.

nodes.name: ensure_review_items
nodes.summary: Ensures every open identity review has a live identity_merge approval item, reopening missing or expired ones, and returns decision-to-approval ids.

nodes.name: scoring.py
nodes.summary: Gate-score-route pipeline for candidate identity pairs: a kind gate blocks human/service/shared merges before any feature is computed, weighted features yield a clamped score, and thresholds route the pair to auto_merge, auto_distinct or review.
nodes.languageNotes: Literal type aliases name the closed gate results and routes; rapidfuzz's JaroWinkler supplies name similarity.

nodes.name: Scored
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass capturing a pair's gate result, feature values, score and route, exactly as written to the decision log.

nodes.name: gate
nodes.summary: Blocks a pair whose account kinds differ when either side is a shared or service account; same-kind pairs pass.

nodes.name: features
nodes.summary: Computes comparison features for two persons: exact email, local-part equals or contained in handle, surname and initial, Jaro-Winkler name similarity, employee id equality and conflicting verified emails.

nodes.name: score
nodes.summary: Sums the configured weights of matched features, using strong and weak Jaro-Winkler bands, and clamps the total to [0, 1].

nodes.name: route
nodes.summary: Routes a score to auto_merge, auto_distinct or review, and never auto-merges when either account kind is unknown.

nodes.name: evaluate
nodes.summary: Runs gate, features, score and route for one pair and returns a Scored result, short-circuiting to blocked when the gate fails.

nodes.name: sync_runs.py
nodes.summary: Records and queries connector sync runs with their per-scope outcomes (complete, partial, or failed with an error class), so that only a scope a run saw completely can turn an absence into a fact (A-118, A-123, A-125).

nodes.name: SyncRun
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass of one connector pull: status, per-scope outcomes, landed and duplicate counts, timing and error details, with a derived error_class.

nodes.name: new_run_id
nodes.summary: Generates a new ULID sync run id.

nodes.name: record
nodes.summary: Inserts a sync run row and one row per scope outcome in a single transaction, truncating long error text.

nodes.name: recent
nodes.summary: Returns the tenant's latest runs newest-first, each with its scopes' status, item counts and details.

nodes.name: ScopeState
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass of how a scope's latest pull left it: status, finish time and run id.

nodes.name: latest_scopes
nodes.summary: Maps every connector:scope to the state its most recent run left it in.

nodes.name: scopes_at
nodes.summary: Resolves the scope states a verdict's manifest names by run id, so a verdict's view of completeness can be reproduced.

nodes.name: last_complete
nodes.summary: Returns when a connector scope was last pulled completely, or None.

nodes.name: written.py
nodes.summary: Writes investigations in code, with no model, for failing tier-1 verdicts the rule already explains: combines lookup results into a root-cause story, renders catalogue fixes for each failing resource, and offers those passing offline checks as suggestions (A-159).

nodes.name: explains
nodes.summary: Decides whether a verdict can be investigated in code: a failed tier-1 verdict that names failing resources for a test with catalogued fixes.

nodes.name: params_for
nodes.summary: Derives a fix's parameters from a failing resource, picking a trail that is not multi-region and logging when the fix keys on trail_name, else using the resource name.

nodes.name: _story
nodes.summary: Summarizes one failing resource's lookups (CloudTrail last change, AWS Config history, Terraform location, skipped or failed reads) as a sentence.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Idempotently writes a code-authored investigation for a verdict: builds stories from lookups, renders and checks each fix, records guardrail events for inapplicable, refused or failing fixes, persists the investigation and suggests the passing fixes.

nodes.name: store.py
nodes.summary: Insert-only access to the lookups table: records what code read about each failing resource (CloudTrail, AWS Config history, infra code) with typed results and raw response ids, and offers credential-free reads for the Investigator and fix suggestions (A-158).

nodes.name: Lookup
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass mirroring one lookups row: verdict, test, resource, kind, params, status, typed result, raw response ids, error and creation time.

nodes.name: _row
nodes.summary: Converts a database row into a Lookup, decoding the JSON params, result and response id columns.

nodes.name: record
nodes.summary: Inserts one lookup row with JSON-encoded params, result and response ids and returns its new ULID.

nodes.name: for_verdict
nodes.summary: Lists a verdict's lookups in creation order.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Fetches one lookup by id, or None.

nodes.name: summary
nodes.summary: Projects a lookup into the Investigator's view, stripping Terraform file text from infra_code results.

nodes.name: failing_of
nodes.summary: Extracts the failing resources (entity id and name) that a verdict's extracted fields named; none for an abstention.

nodes.name: code_files
nodes.summary: Collects the Terraform files, with their text, that successful infra_code lookups found for a resource.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the normalization layer (spec Layer 3), whose pure mappers turn SourceEvents into canonical entities.

nodes.name: aws_mapper.py
nodes.summary: Pure mapper from AWS snapshot events to canonical entities: accounts and S3 buckets become assets with public-access-block and CloudTrail settings, and IAM users become persons with a console and MFA grant on the account (A-140).

nodes.name: account_asset_id
nodes.summary: Builds the deterministic asset entity id for an AWS account.

nodes.name: map_aws_event
nodes.summary: Maps aws.account, aws.s3.bucket and aws.iam.user snapshots to Asset, Person and AccessGrant entities, computing whether a bucket's public access is effectively blocked.

nodes.name: consumer.py
nodes.summary: Normalize-stage consumers: one ordered consumer per raw.<connector> topic reads each raw event back from the raw zone, maps it with the connector's pure mapper, settles revocations on completed pulls, persists entities idempotently and announces them on the entities topic.
nodes.languageNotes: Registers one worker per connector at import time, binding the loop variable through a lambda default argument.

nodes.name: map_event
nodes.summary: Dispatches a SourceEvent to its connector's pure mapper through the MAPPERS registry.

nodes.name: NormalizeConsumer
nodes.summary: OrderedConsumer for one raw connector topic: skips a missing raw file without wedging, maps the event, settles complete-pull revocations, inserts entities and publishes newly inserted ones to the entities topic with step telemetry.

nodes.name: normalize_all
nodes.summary: Drains every raw connector topic for one tenant by running each NormalizeConsumer until idle, returning the number of records processed.

nodes.name: entities.py
nodes.summary: Canonical entity models for normalization (Person, AccessGrant, Asset, Finding, Evidence, Vendor) carrying provenance back to the raw event and deterministic ids, plus the MappingResult every mapper returns.
nodes.languageNotes: Frozen pydantic models with extra='forbid', a closed Entity union type, and a kind property overridden per subclass.

nodes.name: CanonicalBase
nodes.summary: Frozen base model carrying tenant, deterministic entity id and provenance (source connector, source event, observed time) for every canonical entity.

nodes.name: Person
nodes.summary: A person or account as one source saw it: name, emails, handles, employee id, account kind, employment status and owner; partial observations are merged per field later.

nodes.name: AccessGrant
nodes.summary: A person's role on an asset with active or revoked state, its effective time, and source attributes such as MFA.

nodes.name: Asset
nodes.summary: A system or resource (GitHub org or repo, AWS account or bucket, identity provider) with name, type, tags and settings.

nodes.name: Finding
nodes.summary: A finding raised against a test, with severity, summary and subject entity ids.

nodes.name: Evidence
nodes.summary: An evidence document observation: type, title, text, subject, issue date, raw reference, optional per-page texts and methods, and guardrail events.

nodes.name: Vendor
nodes.summary: A third-party vendor with its type and data categories.

nodes.name: MappingResult
nodes.summary: Mapper output bundling entities with any guardrail events raised while mapping, plus an of() filter by entity class.

nodes.name: github_mapper.py
nodes.summary: Pure mapper from GitHub SourceEvents to canonical entities: orgs, repos, members and collaborators become assets, persons and access grants; branch protection, security policies, memberships and file listings become evidence; account kind is inferred from bot type and login patterns.

nodes.name: account_kind_of
nodes.summary: Infers an account kind from GitHub's user type and service-like login patterns (-bot, -svc, ci-, deploy-); shared is never inferred here.

nodes.name: person_id
nodes.summary: Builds the deterministic GitHub person entity id from a node id.

nodes.name: asset_id
nodes.summary: Builds the deterministic GitHub asset entity id from a node id.

nodes.name: grant_id
nodes.summary: Builds the deterministic GitHub grant entity id from person and asset node ids.

nodes.name: _person
nodes.summary: Builds a GitHub Person with its login handle, display name, emails and inferred account kind.

nodes.name: _grant
nodes.summary: Builds a GitHub AccessGrant between a person node and an asset node with role, state and attributes.

nodes.name: _evidence
nodes.summary: Builds a GitHub Evidence entity of a given type with title, text, subject and raw reference.

nodes.name: map_github_event
nodes.summary: Dispatches each GitHub event type (org, member and repo snapshots, branch protection, security policy, file listings, member and collaborator add/remove, pull completion) to entities and guardrail events, flagging files not read and entries not listed.

nodes.name: hris_mapper.py
nodes.summary: Pure mapper from HRIS events to canonical entities: employee snapshots, hires, terminations and role changes become persons with employment status; identity-provider MFA, the account registry, asset tags and documents become assets, grants and evidence; shared accounts come only from an explicit registry kind.

nodes.name: person_id
nodes.summary: Builds the deterministic HRIS person entity id from an employee id.

nodes.name: account_person_id
nodes.summary: Builds the deterministic HRIS account entity id from an account name.

nodes.name: map_hris_event
nodes.summary: Maps each HRIS event type to Person, Asset, AccessGrant, Evidence and Vendor entities with effective timestamps, emitting guardrail events for unknown document or event types.

nodes.name: idp_mapper.py
nodes.summary: Pure mapper from identity-provider user snapshots to a directory asset, a human person keyed by the provider's immutable id, and an SSO grant that is revoked when the user is deprovisioned or suspended, with MFA attributes (A-141).

nodes.name: directory_asset_id
nodes.summary: Builds the deterministic identity-provider directory asset id for a domain.

nodes.name: map_idp_event
nodes.summary: Maps an idp.user.snapshot to the directory Asset, the user's Person and an SSO AccessGrant whose state reflects the provider status, with MFA factors.

nodes.name: manual_mapper.py
nodes.summary: Pure mapper turning a manual evidence upload into exactly one Evidence entity or only guardrail events: ignores tenant claims in manifests and front matter, rejects refused uploads, holds scanned PDFs and images until transcribed, and records how each page's text was obtained (A-96, A-147).

nodes.name: map_manual_event
nodes.summary: Maps manual.refused, plain uploads and manual.transcribed events to Evidence with page texts and methods, or to guardrail events for tenant claims, unreadable PDFs, uploads awaiting transcription and unknown evidence types.

nodes.name: merge.py
nodes.summary: Pure observation-merging rules shared by repository reads and in-memory tests: persons merge per field in time order without letting null or unknown values override known ones, asset settings merge per key, and other entities take the newest observation.

nodes.name: merge_persons
nodes.summary: Merges Person observations per entity in observed order, keeping the latest non-empty value of each field and unioning handles.

nodes.name: merge_assets
nodes.summary: Merges Asset observations per entity, accumulating settings keys across observations onto the newest scalar fields.

nodes.name: latest
nodes.summary: Returns the newest observation per entity id for any canonical entity type.

nodes.name: repository.py
nodes.summary: Entity persistence and current-state reads through ScopedDB: append-only, idempotent observation inserts stamped with the tenant's observation counter, and watermark-aware reads that merge persons and assets and take the newest grants, evidence and vendors.

nodes.name: table_for
nodes.summary: Maps an entity instance to the name of its storage table.

nodes.name: insert
nodes.summary: Inserts one entity observation into its type's table with an observation sequence stamp, returning False when the (entity_id, source_event_id) row already existed.

nodes.name: person_observations
nodes.summary: Loads raw Person observation rows in time order, optionally limited to an observation watermark.

nodes.name: current_persons
nodes.summary: Returns the merged current view of every person, optionally as of a watermark.

nodes.name: current_grants
nodes.summary: Returns the newest observation of every access grant, optionally as of a watermark.

nodes.name: current_assets
nodes.summary: Loads asset observations and merges their settings per key to give the current view of every asset.

nodes.name: current_evidence
nodes.summary: Returns the newest observation of every evidence entity, optionally filtered by evidence type and watermark.

nodes.name: _evidence
nodes.summary: Converts an evidence row into an Evidence model, decoding JSON page texts, guardrail events and page methods.

nodes.name: evidence_version
nodes.summary: Fetches one evidence observation by its source event id (version), or the newest one, for exact version reads.

nodes.name: current_vendors
nodes.summary: Lists current vendors from the current_vendors view.

nodes.name: latest_observed_at
nodes.summary: Returns the most recent observed_at across persons, grants, assets and evidence.

nodes.name: revocations.py
nodes.summary: Settles GitHub access grants from a completed pull's listings: grants on a listing seen whole are reconfirmed or reactivated, and active grants missing from it are revoked at the pull time as new observations, so history keeps every span (A-102, A-119).

nodes.name: listings
nodes.summary: Extracts the org member and repo collaborator listings a pull saw whole as asset id to person id sets, honoring pre-A-119 complete markers.

nodes.name: from_complete_pull
nodes.summary: Compares current GitHub grants with a completed pull's listings and returns new AccessGrant observations for confirmed presence, reappearance and inferred revocation, leaving grants observed at or after the pull alone.

nodes.name: actions.py
nodes.summary: Rule-based remediation fallback that proposes actions from a verdict alone, so the deterministic path never needs a model: removal of surviving GitHub org memberships or repo collaborators for failed HR-1/GH-1 checks and an owner notification for failures or reviews; also re-exports the action catalogue.

nodes.name: ProposalDraft
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass of a proposed remediation action with its target parameters and rationale.

nodes.name: rule_fallback
nodes.summary: Builds proposal drafts from a verdict: remove_org_member or remove_repo_collaborator for each active GitHub grant a failed HR-1/GH-1 verdict cites, plus notify_owner for any failure or needs_review.

nodes.name: documents.py
nodes.summary: Exact reading tools over one evidence version for agents: literal and typed-pattern search (CVE, ARN, email, date, control id), heading and table outlines, bounded span reads, and the chunks covering a span, all with page offsets matching the chunker (A-146).
nodes.languageNotes: Precompiled regex patterns cover CCP control ids plus SOC 2 and ISO 27001 Annex A identifiers.

nodes.name: pages
nodes.summary: Returns an evidence version's (page number, text) pairs, or a single unpaged body.

nodes.name: page_text
nodes.summary: Returns the text of one page (or the whole body when page is None), if present.

nodes.name: Match
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass for a search hit: evidence id, version, type, page, offsets, matched text and surrounding snippet.

nodes.name: find
nodes.summary: Finds case-insensitive literal or typed-pattern matches across evidence in document order, returning up to a limit plus the total count.

nodes.name: Entry
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass for an outline entry (heading or table) with level, title, page and offsets.

nodes.name: _heading
nodes.summary: Recognizes markdown, numbered or upper-case heading lines and returns their level and title.

nodes.name: outline
nodes.summary: Walks each page line by line to list headings and contiguous markdown tables with exact offsets.

nodes.name: Span
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass for an exact text span read: page, offsets, text and a truncation flag.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Returns the exact text between clamped offsets on a page, truncated to MAX_SPAN characters.

nodes.name: covering
nodes.summary: Recomputes the deterministic chunks of an evidence version and returns those overlapping a span on a page.

nodes.name: chunks_of
nodes.summary: Returns every deterministic chunk of an evidence version in order, matching the ids the index holds.

nodes.name: sequences.py
nodes.summary: Per-tenant monotonic counters in tenant_sequences, advanced under a row lock inside the caller's transaction so committed values form exact read watermarks for entity observations and identity rows (A-107, A-125).

nodes.name: next_value
nodes.summary: Upserts and increments a tenant's named counter inside the caller's transaction and returns the new value; the row lock held until commit keeps stamps commit-ordered.

nodes.name: current_value
nodes.summary: Reads the committed value of a tenant counter as a watermark for consistent reads, returning 0 before the first stamp.

nodes.name: types.py
nodes.summary: Closed StrEnum vocabularies (evidence types, account kinds, employment status, grant state, verdict status) shared across every layer; it imports nothing from the package so any module may depend on it.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Python's StrEnum so members compare and serialize as plain strings in SQL rows and JSON payloads.

nodes.name: EvidenceType
nodes.summary: Enumerates the evidence document types (policy documents, training records, HR rosters, repo settings, file listings, MFA status, account registry, cloud configuration and more) that Evidence entities and evaluators key on.

nodes.name: AccountKind
nodes.summary: Classifies an account as human, service, shared or unknown; drives the identity-resolution gate that refuses to merge humans with service or shared accounts.

nodes.name: EmploymentStatus
nodes.summary: HR employment status vocabulary (active, terminated, unknown) carried on Person entities and used by termination checks.

nodes.name: GrantState
nodes.summary: Access grant lifecycle state: active or revoked.

nodes.name: VerdictStatus
nodes.summary: Evaluator verdict outcomes: pass, fail, partial and needs_review.

nodes.name: cli.py
nodes.summary: Typer sub-app for `ccp investigate`: runs the Investigator over every pending fail/needs_review verdict (or one verdict id) and shows or lists stored investigations as JSON or one-line rows.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: CLI command that requires an Anthropic key, then either investigates one named verdict and prints it or drains the investigator queue and prints consumed, queued, investigated, parked and skipped counts plus rejected targets.

nodes.name: show
nodes.summary: CLI command printing the stored investigation for one verdict as JSON, exiting 1 when there is none.

nodes.name: list_cmd
nodes.summary: CLI command listing every stored investigation with its root-cause category, verdict id and number of proposed actions.

nodes.name: _render
nodes.summary: Serializes an Investigation (root cause, category, missing evidence, proposed actions, confidence, guardrail events) to indented JSON for the terminal.

nodes.name: runner.py
nodes.summary: The Investigator runner (Layer 14): an ordered consumer of the verdicts topic queues one parallel investigation job per fail/needs_review verdict; each job runs the investigator LangGraph agent on a resumable per-verdict thread, persists the Investigation, revalidates proposed targets, writes remediation proposals and offline-checked fix suggestions, and opens evidence-request approvals.
nodes.languageNotes: A deterministic checkpoint thread id per verdict lets a retried job resume from its last LangGraph checkpoint instead of repeating model calls; both consumers register with the worker at import time via register(...).

nodes.name: RunSummary
nodes.summary: Dataclass of counters for a drain pass: verdicts consumed, jobs enqueued, investigations run and how many code wrote, skipped, parked, proposals, evidence requests and rejected targets.

nodes.name: thread_id_of
nodes.summary: Derives the deterministic checkpoint thread id `<tenant>:investigate:<verdict>:run` so a retried job finds its own run (A-109).

nodes.name: _build
nodes.summary: Assembles the investigator graph: a run budget tracker, read-only agent-role tool bindings behind the authz Gate, model deps for the investigator model, and a tenant-scoped checkpoint saver; returns the compiled graph, the pools to close and the tracker.

nodes.name: investigate
nodes.summary: Runs the investigator graph for one verdict end to end: returns an existing investigation, enforces the daily budget, creates or resumes the agent thread, streams the graph inside an observability step, finishes and records spend, and marks the thread finished, cancelled or failed.

nodes.name: _finish
nodes.summary: Turns the graph's final state into a persisted Investigation: revalidates each proposed action target (rejections become guardrail events), writes or reuses remediation proposal rows, records model-chosen fixes as suggestions, and opens an evidence_request approval when evidence is missing.

nodes.name: _render_fixes
nodes.summary: Renders the model's fix choices in code against the verdict's lookup results and offers only those passing the offline checks; refusals and failed checks become guardrail events (A-160).

nodes.name: _proposal_row
nodes.summary: Reuses an existing remediation proposal for the same action and target (such as a rule fallback) or creates a new investigator-sourced remediation_proposals row.

nodes.name: InvestigationsConsumer
nodes.summary: Ordered consumer of the verdicts topic that, with no model call, queues one `investigations` job per fail/needs_review verdict without an investigation, skipping verdicts whose lookup plan queues them later and redelivered verdicts already queued.

nodes.name: InvestigationJobs
nodes.summary: Parallel consumer running one investigation per job outside any transaction, one per verdict at a time: lets code write the explanation when the rule explains the verdict, parks without a model key or over budget, and tallies proposals, evidence requests and rejected targets.

nodes.name: drain
nodes.summary: Drains the investigator queue, unparks parked jobs once a model key is configured, runs the queued jobs and returns the RunSummary.

nodes.name: cli.py
nodes.summary: Typer sub-app for `ccp lookups`: runs the pre-investigation reads about failing resources and prints what they found for one verdict (A-158).

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: CLI command that drains the lookups runner for a tenant and prints how many jobs were queued, looked up, landed and handed to investigation.

nodes.name: show
nodes.summary: CLI command printing a JSON summary of every lookup stored for one verdict.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the observability layer (the JSONL step logger, with Langfuse emission added later); it holds only a docstring.

nodes.name: steps.py
nodes.summary: The step logger (Layer 12): a `step()` context manager writes one JSON line per step to logs/steps.jsonl with OpenTelemetry gen_ai.* and ccp.* attributes, masks secrets, offloads payloads over 4 KB to blob files, prices model usage, and mirrors the record to a Langfuse sink whose failure never loses the local record.
nodes.languageNotes: ContextVars carry the run id, parent step and current record, so nested `with step(...)` blocks form a tree and model calls deep inside agents are attributed to the enclosing step without passing it explicitly.

nodes.name: configure
nodes.summary: Points the step log at the settings' logs directory and builds the tracing sink (auto via tracing.build_sink, explicit, or none); prints and returns a warning when Langfuse is configured but unreachable.

nodes.name: set_sink
nodes.summary: Replaces the module-level tracing sink, or turns tracing off with None.

nodes.name: sink_active
nodes.summary: Reports whether a tracing sink is currently configured.

nodes.name: log_path
nodes.summary: Returns the current steps.jsonl path; the eval runner reads usage back from it.

nodes.name: blobs_dir
nodes.summary: Returns the blobs directory beside the step log where large inputs and outputs are offloaded.

nodes.name: new_run
nodes.summary: Mints a ULID run id and binds it to the current context so later steps nest under it.

nodes.name: current_run_id
nodes.summary: Returns the run id bound to the current context, if any.

nodes.name: StepRecord
nodes.summary: Mutable dataclass for one step: ids, layer, tenant, inputs and output, model with prompt version and hash, gen_ai usage fields, guardrail events and error; its methods set the output and model, set or accumulate usage, add events and price the usage in USD.

nodes.name: note_model_call
nodes.summary: Attributes a model call's tokens and prompt version to the step active in the current context, so cost accounting sees agent and judge calls, not only tier 2's.

nodes.name: _offload
nodes.summary: Writes a step's inputs or output over 4 KB to logs/blobs/{step_id}.{kind}.json and returns a `$blob` reference with the byte size; smaller values pass through unchanged.

nodes.name: resolve_blobs
nodes.summary: Returns a step line with any offloaded inputs or output read back from their blob files.

nodes.name: read_lines
nodes.summary: Iterates the step log as parsed dicts with blobs resolved, skipping malformed lines.

nodes.name: step
nodes.summary: Context manager that opens a StepRecord nested under the current parent step and run, starts a sink observation, and on exit always appends the masked, offloaded, priced JSON line and ends the observation; a failing sink turns tracing off instead of blocking the record.

nodes.name: flush
nodes.summary: Flushes the tracing sink, turning tracing off if the flush raises.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the Policy Agent (Layer 15), documenting that gap analysis and drafts run over policy_document evidence and that drafts go to the approval stage without ever becoming evidence.

nodes.name: cli.py
nodes.summary: Typer sub-app for `ccp policy gap|draft|drafts`: runs Policy Agent gap analysis or Markdown drafting for one control, exits with code 3 when the run is parked over budget, and lists stored drafts.

nodes.name: _render
nodes.summary: Serializes a GapReport (id, control, summary, confidence, gaps, guardrail events) as indented JSON.

nodes.name: gap
nodes.summary: CLI command running gap analysis for one control and printing the report; a parked run exits with code 3.

nodes.name: draft
nodes.summary: CLI command running draft mode for one control and printing the gap report, the draft path, its approval id and any scrubbed cross-tenant tokens.

nodes.name: drafts
nodes.summary: CLI command listing stored policy drafts, optionally for one control, with path and approval id.

nodes.name: runner.py
nodes.summary: The Policy runner (Layer 15): builds the policy LangGraph for a tenant and control with evidence search pinned to policy_document, runs it in gap or draft mode under budget and observability, persists the GapReport, and in draft mode writes write-once Markdown under data/drafts/<tenant>/ with its SHA-256 and opens a policy_draft approval.

nodes.name: other_tenant_tokens
nodes.summary: Collects distinctive names of every other configured tenant (display name, GitHub org, id and non-generic name words), longest first, so a draft for one tenant can be scrubbed of the others (S9).

nodes.name: _build
nodes.summary: Assembles the policy graph: budget tracker, read-only tool bindings with evidence search pinned to policy_document, the authz gate, policy model deps, forbidden cross-tenant tokens and a tenant-scoped checkpoint saver.

nodes.name: _run
nodes.summary: Runs the policy graph in gap or draft mode for a known control: checks the model key and daily budget, creates a thread, streams the graph inside a policy step, records harness events and spend, and marks the thread finished or failed.

nodes.name: _report_from
nodes.summary: Builds a GapReport from the graph's final state, validating each gap's covering citations.

nodes.name: gap
nodes.summary: Gap mode entry point: runs the graph, then builds, persists and returns the GapReport.

nodes.name: draft
nodes.summary: Draft mode entry point: runs the graph, persists the report, writes the Markdown draft exclusively (never overwriting) under the tenant's drafts directory, hashes it, opens a policy_draft approval item and persists the PolicyDraft.

nodes.name: schema.py
nodes.summary: Pydantic records for the Policy Agent (PolicyGap, GapReport, PolicyDraft) and their persistence to the gap_reports and policy_drafts tables through ScopedDB.

nodes.name: PolicyGap
nodes.summary: Frozen Pydantic model for one requirement's coverage: requirement id, covered flag, verified covering citations and a gap description.

nodes.name: GapReport
nodes.summary: Frozen Pydantic model of a control's gap analysis: gaps, summary, bounded confidence and cap, model and prompt version, guardrail events, thread id and raw request/response; `uncovered` lists uncovered requirement ids.

nodes.name: PolicyDraft
nodes.summary: Frozen Pydantic model of a Markdown policy draft: control, source report, addressed requirements, the file path and approval id the runner sets, and scrub events.

nodes.name: persist_report
nodes.summary: Inserts a GapReport into gap_reports, JSON-encoding gaps, events and the model request/response.

nodes.name: _report
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a GapReport from a gap_reports row, decoding its JSON columns.

nodes.name: latest_report
nodes.summary: Fetches the newest GapReport for a control.

nodes.name: get_report
nodes.summary: Fetches one GapReport by id.

nodes.name: persist_draft
nodes.summary: Inserts a PolicyDraft row with its Markdown SHA-256 into policy_drafts.

nodes.name: list_drafts
nodes.summary: Lists policy drafts newest first, optionally for one control, as plain dicts.

nodes.name: cli.py
nodes.summary: Typer sub-app for `ccp questionnaires`: creates a questionnaire from YAML, drafts answers through the fixed pipeline, shows, approves or rejects answers, sweeps stale ones, records that a person sent it, and prints metrics (A-163).

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: CLI command loading a YAML questionnaire (title, requester, questions) and storing it, printing the new id.

nodes.name: answer
nodes.summary: CLI command drafting every question without a live answer through the questionnaire pipeline.

nodes.name: show
nodes.summary: CLI command printing each answer's question id, status, answer, failed checks and final text.

nodes.name: approve
nodes.summary: CLI command approving a drafted answer, optionally with the reviewer's edited text.

nodes.name: reject
nodes.summary: CLI command rejecting a drafted answer with a reviewer note.

nodes.name: stale
nodes.summary: CLI command sweeping answers whose evidence has gone stale and printing how many were marked.

nodes.name: send_cmd
nodes.summary: CLI command recording that a person sent the questionnaire; it fails unless every answer is approved and current.

nodes.name: metrics
nodes.summary: CLI command printing questionnaire metrics as JSON.

nodes.name: confirm.py
nodes.summary: Confirms suggested fixes only from evidence (A-160): a verdicts-topic consumer marks suggestions confirmed when a later read passes or no longer names the resource and reopened when it fails again within 30 days; it also records human accept/dismiss decisions, which never confirm, and computes the LT1 metrics.

nodes.name: _event
nodes.summary: Inserts a CCP-authored fix_suggestion_events row (confirmed or reopened) on the consumer's cursor.

nodes.name: _still_failing
nodes.summary: Decides whether a verdict still fails for a resource: only failed verdicts count, and a failure that names no resources covers every resource.

nodes.name: settle
nodes.summary: For a passed or failed verdict, finds earlier suggestions for the same test and subject made before its evidence was observed, confirms live ones the read sees fixed, and reopens confirmed ones failing again within 30 days.

nodes.name: FixConfirmations
nodes.summary: Ordered verdicts-topic consumer ('fix-confirmations') that settles suggestions from each new verdict and counts confirmations and reopenings; it never confirms from a person.

nodes.name: drain
nodes.summary: Runs the fix-confirmations consumer until nothing is left and returns it with its counts.

nodes.name: decide
nodes.summary: Records a person's accepted or dismissed decision on a live suggestion, requiring a note for dismissals; neither confirms the fix.

nodes.name: Metrics
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass of LT1 numbers: suggestions by status, median hours from failing verdict to confirming read, confirmed and reopened counts, with a derived reopen rate.

nodes.name: metrics
nodes.summary: Computes LT1 metrics from fix suggestion status and events joined to verdicts, optionally only since a timestamp.

nodes.name: fix_cli.py
nodes.summary: Typer sub-app for `ccp fixes`: lists and shows the fixes CCP suggests (Terraform diff, commands, console steps, done-when check), records accept/dismiss decisions, runs confirmation from new verdicts, and prints LT1 metrics; CCP never applies a fix itself.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Formats a Suggestion for the terminal: header, title and fix version, Terraform diff, commands, console steps and the 'done when' verification.

nodes.name: list_
nodes.summary: CLI command listing suggestions, optionally filtered by status or test.

nodes.name: show
nodes.summary: CLI command printing one rendered suggestion.

nodes.name: _decide
nodes.summary: Shared body of accept and dismiss: records the decision through confirm.decide and reminds that only a later read confirms the fix.

nodes.name: accept
nodes.summary: CLI command recording that a person will apply the fix.

nodes.name: dismiss
nodes.summary: CLI command dismissing a suggestion with a required reason.

nodes.name: confirm_cmd
nodes.summary: CLI command draining the fix-confirmations consumer and printing confirmed and reopened counts.

nodes.name: metrics
nodes.summary: CLI command printing the LT1 fix metrics (by status, median hours to confirmation, reopen rate) as JSON.

nodes.name: suggestions.py
nodes.summary: Append-only fix suggestion records (A-159): an immutable Suggestion row holds the rendered fix and its payload hash, every status change (open, accepted, dismissed, confirmed, reopened, superseded) is an event, and one live suggestion exists per test, resource and fix.

nodes.name: Suggestion
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass mirroring a fix_suggestion_status row: the rendered fix (template version and hash, params, body, checks, lookups, payload hash) plus its latest status, actor, note and time.

nodes.name: _row
nodes.summary: Maps a fix_suggestion_status row tuple to a Suggestion, decoding its JSON columns.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Loads one suggestion with its current status.

nodes.name: list_all
nodes.summary: Lists suggestions newest first, optionally filtered by status and test, up to a limit.

nodes.name: for_verdict
nodes.summary: Lists the suggestions raised for one verdict in creation order.

nodes.name: live_for
nodes.summary: Lists the suggestions for a test and resource still waiting for a read that sees the fix (open, accepted or reopened).

nodes.name: record_event
nodes.summary: Appends a status-change event for a suggestion with actor, note and optional verdict id.

nodes.name: suggest
nodes.summary: Offers a rendered fix: refuses renderings that failed an offline check, returns the existing suggestion for an identical payload, supersedes older renderings of the same fix, and inserts a new suggestion with an open event.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the storage layer: Postgres connections, migrations and the tenant-scoped query surface.

nodes.name: checkpoints.py
nodes.summary: LangGraph Postgres checkpoint tables under row-level security: admin setup creates the saver's tables in a checkpoints schema with a thread-id-prefix tenant policy, and the app-side saver runs every statement in a transaction that sets app.tenant_id locally (A-99).
nodes.languageNotes: tenant_saver defines a PostgresSaver subclass inside the function to override its private `_cursor`, closing over the tenant so each transaction runs set_config('app.tenant_id', ..., true) first.

nodes.name: setup_checkpoint_tables
nodes.summary: As the admin role, runs PostgresSaver.setup() in the checkpoints schema, grants the app role access, and enables and forces RLS with a tenant_isolation policy comparing the thread id's first segment to app_tenant().

nodes.name: saver_conninfo
nodes.summary: Builds the saver's connection string with search_path=checkpoints and no session-level tenant.

nodes.name: saver_pool
nodes.summary: Opens a psycopg pool for the saver with autocommit, no prepared statements and dict rows.

nodes.name: tenant_saver
nodes.summary: Returns a PostgresSaver whose every cursor runs inside a transaction that first sets app.tenant_id for that transaction only.

nodes.name: thread_id_for
nodes.summary: Mints a thread id `<tenant>:<test>:<subject>:<run>` whose tenant prefix the RLS policy and CLI guard rely on.

nodes.name: tenant_of_thread
nodes.summary: Extracts the tenant id prefix from a thread id.

nodes.name: db.py
nodes.summary: Database connections and the add-only migration runner: app, read-only agent and replica pools with PgBouncer-safe session settings, lag-bounded read routing, role hardening (NOBYPASSRLS), migrations applied exactly once, checkpoint table setup, scratch databases for tests and evals, the RLS lint entry, and a server check.

nodes.name: admin_connection
nodes.summary: Opens an autocommit connection as the admin role, for the migration runner and tests only.

nodes.name: app_pool
nodes.summary: Creates the application-role connection pool, the only route from app code to Postgres.

nodes.name: listen_url
nodes.summary: Returns the direct database URL for LISTEN, which a transaction pooler cannot serve.

nodes.name: replica_pool
nodes.summary: Creates a read-only replica pool when a replica URL is configured (A-172).

nodes.name: replica_lag
nodes.summary: Measures replica replay lag in seconds: 0 when the server is not replaying, None when it cannot be asked.

nodes.name: read_pool
nodes.summary: Routes a lag-tolerant read to the replica while its lag is within the configured bound, otherwise to the primary.

nodes.name: agent_url
nodes.summary: Returns the agent tools' read-only role URL, defaulting to the application URL with user ccp_agent (A-115).

nodes.name: agent_pool
nodes.summary: Creates a pool on the read-only agent role with a 15-second statement timeout.

nodes.name: Pools
nodes.summary: Groups the connection pools a run opens together so they are closed together.

nodes.name: app_role_and_password
nodes.summary: Parses the application role name and password from DATABASE_URL.

nodes.name: agent_role_and_password
nodes.summary: Parses the agent role name and password from the agent URL.

nodes.name: _ensure_app_role
nodes.summary: Creates a login role with NOSUPERUSER and NOBYPASSRLS, or re-hardens an existing one, then grants it CONNECT on the database.

nodes.name: migrate
nodes.summary: As admin, ensures and hardens the app and agent roles, applies unapplied migrations in name order with role placeholders substituted, records them in schema_migrations, then sets up the RLS-guarded checkpoint tables.

nodes.name: scratch_database
nodes.summary: Context manager that creates a uniquely named throwaway database, migrates it, yields settings pointing at it and force-drops it afterwards.

nodes.name: lint_catalogue
nodes.summary: Runs the RLS catalogue lint as the admin role against the app and agent roles.

nodes.name: check
nodes.summary: Connects as the app role and reports server version, pgvector version, whether the role bypasses RLS or is superuser, and how many migrations are applied.

nodes.name: lint.py
nodes.summary: Row-level security catalogue lint (A-99): for every tenant table it checks RLS is enabled and forced, the only policy is a permissive tenant_isolation filtering reads and writes, insert-only tables deny UPDATE/DELETE and every table is classified; it also pins dispatch-table columns and checks the agent role is read-only.
nodes.languageNotes: It inspects the live Postgres catalogs (pg_class, pg_policies, information_schema.role_table_grants) rather than parsing migration files, so it validates what was actually applied.

nodes.name: Finding
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass naming a table and the lint problem found, printed as 'table: problem'.

nodes.name: _tenant_tables
nodes.summary: Lists non-partition tables scoped by tenant_id in public or thread_id in checkpoints, with their RLS enabled and forced flags.

nodes.name: _agent_role
nodes.summary: Checks the agent role exists, is neither superuser nor RLS-bypassing, and holds no INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE grants.

nodes.name: lint
nodes.summary: Runs every catalogue check and returns findings: agent role, dispatch-table column pins, RLS forced, exactly one correctly predicated tenant_isolation policy, insert-only privileges and table classification.

nodes.name: cli.py
nodes.summary: Typer sub-app for `ccp tasks`: plans long tasks (audit_prep, questionnaire) as typed item rows, advances them pass by pass (optionally draining fanned-out item jobs), shows, lists, resolves, cancels, resumes and answers items, and measures single versus fan-out runs (A-150).

nodes.name: _show
nodes.summary: Formats a task header (status, spend against cap and forecast, deadline, passes) and one line per item with status, outcome, attempts and open question.

nodes.name: plan
nodes.summary: CLI command writing a task's items from scoping facts (framework and families for audit_prep, a YAML question file for questionnaires); no model runs.

nodes.name: advance
nodes.summary: CLI command running one task pass with the launcher's reader, optionally draining queued item jobs, and printing the pass summary and events.

nodes.name: show
nodes.summary: CLI command printing a task and its items, optionally with every task event.

nodes.name: list_
nodes.summary: CLI command listing tasks with kind, status and spend against cap.

nodes.name: gaps
nodes.summary: CLI command printing the task's gap list as JSON rows.

nodes.name: resolve
nodes.summary: CLI command letting a person settle an item held for review.

nodes.name: cancel
nodes.summary: CLI command cancelling a task with a reason.

nodes.name: resume
nodes.summary: CLI command reopening a parked task, optionally with a new deadline or dollar cap.

nodes.name: measure
nodes.summary: CLI command running a labelled questionnaire fixture in single or fan-out mode and printing the scored record; it needs a model key.

nodes.name: answer
nodes.summary: CLI command answering a waiting item's open question so the next pass picks it up (A-154).

nodes.name: launcher.py
nodes.summary: The task fan-out launcher (A-151): reads open task items either as one queued parallel run per item on the task_items topic or as a single inline run over a batch, runs the task_item LangGraph with a budget lowered to what the task has left, merges each typed reading into its item by code rules, and measures single-run baselines that gate fan-out.
nodes.languageNotes: Import-time side effects register TaskItemJobs with the worker and install the 'tasks' job in evaluators.jobs.JOBS; reader() returns a closure that caches providers between calls.

nodes.name: KindsConfig
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass of config/task_kinds.yaml: the single-run item limit and per-kind fan-out flags.

nodes.name: load_kinds
nodes.summary: Loads task_kinds.yaml, with defaults when it is absent, into a KindsConfig.

nodes.name: baselines
nodes.summary: Loads a kind's recorded single-run measurement files, oldest first.

nodes.name: fanout_enabled
nodes.summary: Allows fan-out for a kind only when config enables it and a single-run baseline has been recorded.

nodes.name: RunResult
nodes.summary: Dataclass of one run's id, USD and tokens spent, per-item merged statuses, rejections and guardrail events.

nodes.name: run_id_for
nodes.summary: Mints a tenant-prefixed run id from the task, the item or batch label and the attempt, so a retried job resumes its own run.

nodes.name: _items_payload
nodes.summary: Builds typed per-item state for a run (question, inputs, cited evidence ids, newest human answer) and never an earlier run's messages.

nodes.name: run_items
nodes.summary: Runs one fresh task_item graph over the given items with a budget capped at the task's remaining dollars, resumable checkpointing, stop watching and an observability step, then charges the task and merges each item's reading.

nodes.name: merge
nodes.summary: Applies code rules to one item's reading: no reading, a stopped loop, a failed correction, an unsupported or answer-only claim go to needs_review; insufficient evidence waits with an open question; otherwise final; records the run event and evidence ids.

nodes.name: _hold
nodes.summary: Marks an item needs_review with a reason after its run failed or was stopped.

nodes.name: _start
nodes.summary: Marks an item running, increments its attempts and records the run id.

nodes.name: _exhausted
nodes.summary: Holds items at their run limit for a person and returns the ones still allowed to run.

nodes.name: launch
nodes.summary: Fan-out mode: marks each runnable item running and appends one task_items job per item to the event log.

nodes.name: single
nodes.summary: Single-run mode: runs one graph inline over up to `limit` runnable items and reports merged statuses, holding every item when the run is stopped or over budget.

nodes.name: reader
nodes.summary: Builds the Reader the task runner hands open reads to: fan-out when the kind may, otherwise a single run; without a model key reads are parked and items stay open.

nodes.name: TaskItemJobs
nodes.summary: Parallel consumer running one fanned-out item per job: skips superseded attempts, reopens or cancels items of parked or cancelled tasks, parks without a model key, and holds a failed item alone.

nodes.name: drain
nodes.summary: Runs every queued task item job for the tenant and returns (item id, status) pairs.

nodes.name: measure
nodes.summary: Plans a labelled questionnaire task, advances it in single or fan-out mode, scores each item's outcome against its label, and writes the record (accuracy, cost, statuses, bundle id) to the eval runs directory.

nodes.name: conftest.py
nodes.summary: Shared pytest fixtures: resets connector rate buckets before each test and provides session-scoped settings with tracing disabled, a migrated scratch database (skipped when Postgres is unreachable) and an app-role pool.

nodes.name: base_settings
nodes.summary: Session fixture creating settings over a temporary data directory and configuring the step logger with no tracing sink.

nodes.name: db_settings
nodes.summary: Session fixture yielding settings for a migrated scratch database, skipping db tests when Postgres is unreachable.

nodes.name: pool
nodes.summary: Session fixture yielding an application-role connection pool on the scratch database.

nodes.name: test_tenant_keys_and_rls_lint.py
nodes.summary: NT9 (A-99) security tests: the RLS catalogue lint passes and classifies every tenant table, fails on permissive policies and opened audit tables, cross-tenant foreign-key references are rejected, caches key by tenant, and the checkpoint saver scopes statements by a transaction-local tenant.

nodes.name: migrated
nodes.summary: Module fixture yielding a migrated scratch database, skipping when Postgres is unreachable.

nodes.name: test_the_lint_passes_and_covers_every_tenant_table
nodes.summary: Asserts the lint reports nothing on the migrated schema and every public tenant_id table is classified insert-only, operational or dispatch.

nodes.name: test_a_permissive_policy_fails_the_lint
nodes.summary: Negative controls: an extra permissive policy, an unclassified table, unforced RLS and an UPDATE grant on verdicts each produce lint findings.

nodes.name: test_a_reference_to_another_tenants_row_is_rejected
nodes.summary: Asserts compliance_state and remediation_proposals rows referencing another tenant's verdict raise ForeignKeyViolation, while a same-tenant reference succeeds.

nodes.name: test_the_caches_are_keyed_by_tenant
nodes.summary: Asserts two tenants caching the same embedding and enrichment keys each read back their own values.
