nodes.languageNotes: app_tenant() raises instead of returning an empty string because current_setting(..., true) reads as '' after any SET LOCAL in a pooled session; event_log uses GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY offsets and a partial index for parallel claiming.

nodes.name: 0002_rls.sql
nodes.summary: Grants the templated {{app_role}} least-privilege access to the Phase 0 tables (SELECT and INSERT only on append-only ones) and turns on FORCE row-level security with a tenant_isolation policy on raw_events, event_log and dead_letter.
nodes.languageNotes: FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY together with a NOBYPASSRLS, non-owner app role means the tenant policy applies to every application query.

nodes.name: 0003_entities.sql
nodes.summary: Phase 3 canonical entity schema: append-only observation tables for persons, access_grants, assets, evidence, vendors and findings, plus SECURITY INVOKER current_* views that pick each entity's latest observation, all under tenant row-level security.
nodes.languageNotes: DISTINCT ON (tenant_id, entity_id) ordered by observed_at DESC derives current state from an append-only log; security_invoker views keep RLS evaluated as the querying role rather than the view owner.

nodes.name: 0004_identity.sql
nodes.summary: Phase 4 identity-resolution schema: resolution_decisions records every scored candidate pair, person_links maps entities to canonical persons, and review_queue and review_resolutions hold human review, with derived current_person_links and open_review_queue views.

nodes.name: 0005_state.sql
nodes.summary: Phase 5 migration creating the append-only verdicts table (keeping the exact model request and response for replay), per-tenant tenant_sequences counters, and the bitemporal compliance_state table whose corrections supersede earlier rows; UPDATE and DELETE are revoked from the app role.
nodes.languageNotes: Bitemporal design: valid_from/valid_to carry valid time while recorded_seq, stamped under a per-tenant lock, carries transaction time; a partial unique index lets a row be superseded at most once.

nodes.name: 0006_knowledge.sql
nodes.summary: Phase 6 knowledge-graph reference tables (frameworks, requirements, controls, tests and the requirement_controls and control_tests join tables); they hold no tenant data, so they have no tenant_id or RLS and are the one place the loader may upsert.

nodes.name: 0007_evaluations.sql
nodes.summary: Phase 7a evaluation bookkeeping: adds verdicts.trigger_reason (why an evaluation ran) and creates the append-only spend_ledger behind the per-tenant daily model budget gate.

nodes.name: 0008_chunks.sql
nodes.summary: Phase 7b retrieval index: the chunks table with a generated tsvector, a 1024-dimension pgvector embedding and GIN/HNSW indexes, plus content-hash keyed embedding_cache and enrichment_cache tables.
nodes.languageNotes: Hybrid retrieval in one table: a STORED generated tsvector with a GIN index for full text and a pgvector HNSW index with vector_cosine_ops for semantic search.

nodes.name: 0009_agent.sql
nodes.summary: Phase 8 agent runtime bookkeeping: creates the checkpoints schema that LangGraph's PostgresSaver fills and the agent_threads table tracking each tier-3 graph run's status, interrupt payload, resuming human decision and resulting verdict.

nodes.name: 0010_agent_trajectory.sql
nodes.summary: One-statement Phase 8 migration adding a trajectory column to agent_threads that records the node sequence a graph run took, for trajectory tests and the CLI inspect view.

nodes.name: 0011_remediation_approvals.sql
nodes.summary: Phases 10-11 schema for remediation proposals and the shared human approval stage: remediation_proposals, append-only approvals and approval_events, and the approval_status view that derives each item's state from its latest event.
nodes.languageNotes: JOIN LATERAL (... ORDER BY recorded_at DESC LIMIT 1) projects current state from an append-only event table; later migrations reuse this pattern for proposals, fix suggestions and questionnaire answers.

nodes.name: 0012_investigations.sql
nodes.summary: Phase 12 append-only investigations table recording what the Investigator agent concluded about one verdict: root cause and category, missing evidence, proposed actions, citations, capped confidence and the exact model exchange.

nodes.name: 0013_policy.sql
nodes.summary: Phase 13 Policy Agent outputs: append-only gap_reports per control and policy_drafts registering on-disk draft markdown with its hash, addressed requirements and approval item; a draft never becomes evidence on its own.

nodes.name: 0014_copilot.sql
nodes.summary: Phase 14 append-only copilot_answers table, one row per Copilot turn with intent, cited answer text, requested actions, latency figures and the raw model exchange.

nodes.name: 0015_review_indexes.sql
nodes.summary: Review fix-up adding missing indexes on policy_drafts, a foreign key from policy_drafts to approvals, and a unique thread/turn index on copilot_answers that enforces one row per turn.

nodes.name: 0016_approval_hardening.sql
nodes.summary: NT2 fail-closed approvals: stores the exact decision on approval_events, adds the remediation_rollback approval kind, and redefines approval_status so the decision travels with the latest event.

nodes.name: raw_events
nodes.summary: Append-only record of every landed source event, keyed by tenant, connector and source event id for de-duplication, pointing at the raw payload by path and digest (later with stored digest, version id and store).

nodes.name: event_log
nodes.summary: The Postgres Kafka stand-in: an identity-offset log of topic records with partition keys and claim status, later extended with retry, lease and per-topic seq columns for parallel and ordered consumers.

nodes.name: consumer_offsets
nodes.summary: Cursor table for ordered-topic consumers, one row per consumer and topic; its cursor moved from offsets to per-tenant seq in MT2.

nodes.name: dead_letter
nodes.summary: Append-only dead-letter record of event_log entries that exhausted their attempts, with the last error.

nodes.name: persons
nodes.summary: Append-only person observations from connectors: display name, emails, handles, employee id, account kind and employment status.

nodes.name: access_grants
nodes.summary: Append-only observations of a person's role on an asset, active or revoked, with when that state took effect.

nodes.name: assets
nodes.summary: Append-only asset observations (repositories and other resources) with type, tags and settings snapshots.

nodes.name: evidence
nodes.summary: Append-only evidence observations: typed documents with text, optional page texts and page methods, subject, issue date, raw reference and guardrail events.

nodes.name: vendors
nodes.summary: Append-only vendor observations with vendor type and the data categories they handle.

nodes.name: findings
nodes.summary: Append-only finding observations with test id, severity, summary and affected subject entities.

nodes.name: current_persons
nodes.summary: SECURITY INVOKER view returning each person entity's latest observation.

nodes.name: current_access_grants
nodes.summary: SECURITY INVOKER view returning each access grant's latest observation.

nodes.name: current_assets
nodes.summary: SECURITY INVOKER view returning each asset's latest observation; the repository layer merges settings across observations.

nodes.name: current_evidence
nodes.summary: SECURITY INVOKER view returning each evidence entity's latest observation.

nodes.name: current_vendors
nodes.summary: SECURITY INVOKER view returning each vendor's latest observation.

nodes.name: resolution_decisions
nodes.summary: Append-only record of every scored identity candidate pair: block keys, gate result, compared features, score, route and the thresholds in force.

nodes.name: person_links
nodes.summary: Append-only links mapping a person entity to its canonical person, decided by auto-merge or a human and tied to the resolution decision.

nodes.name: review_queue
nodes.summary: Identity pairs routed to human review; an item stays open until a resolution row references it.

nodes.name: review_resolutions
nodes.summary: Append-only human outcomes (merge or distinct) for review-queue items, with reviewer, note and later the identity_merge approval item.

nodes.name: current_person_links
nodes.summary: SECURITY INVOKER view returning the latest canonical link per person entity.

nodes.name: open_review_queue
nodes.summary: SECURITY INVOKER view listing review-queue items that have no resolution yet.

nodes.name: verdicts
nodes.summary: Append-only evaluation results per test and subject: status, reasoning, citations, capped confidence, tier, model, prompt and rule version, retrieved chunk ids, manifest, bundle and the exact model request and response for replay.

nodes.name: tenant_sequences
nodes.summary: Per-tenant named monotonic counters locked by writers so recorded order equals commit order; used for transaction time, observation watermarks and topic seq.

nodes.name: compliance_state
nodes.summary: Bitemporal compliance-state rows per subject: status with valid time and a per-tenant recorded_seq transaction time; corrections, overrides, late events and rule changes supersede earlier rows rather than editing them.

nodes.name: frameworks
nodes.summary: Reference list of compliance frameworks.

nodes.name: requirements
nodes.summary: Framework requirements with title, intent and clauses.

nodes.name: controls
nodes.summary: Reference controls with title and description, mapped to requirements and tests.

nodes.name: tests
nodes.summary: Test catalogue: deterministic or interpretive evaluation, evidence types, subject kind, rule, valid-from strategy, tier and the full test spec.

nodes.name: requirement_controls
nodes.summary: Join table mapping framework requirements to the controls that satisfy them.

nodes.name: control_tests
nodes.summary: Join table mapping controls to the tests that evaluate them.

nodes.name: spend_ledger
nodes.summary: Append-only per-tenant model spend entries (dollars and tokens) behind the daily budget gate.

nodes.name: chunks
nodes.summary: Serving projection of the retrieval index: content-hash chunk ids over current evidence with a generated tsvector, a 1024-dimension embedding, distractor flag and later generation and offsets; the one tenant table the app may update and delete.

nodes.name: embedding_cache
nodes.summary: Content-hash keyed cache of embeddings per tenant and embedding model.

nodes.name: enrichment_cache
nodes.summary: Content-hash keyed cache of contextual chunk enrichment per tenant, model and prompt version.

nodes.name: agent_threads
nodes.summary: One row per agent graph run: status, interrupt payload, resuming human decision and produced verdict, later extended with trajectory, evaluation key, input state and bundle id.

nodes.name: remediation_proposals
nodes.summary: Remediation proposals per verdict (rule, investigator, copilot or rollback source) with target, rationale, reversibility, risk, precondition and payload hash; insert-only since MT4, with status moved to proposal_events.

nodes.name: approvals
nodes.summary: Append-only approval items of every kind (tier-3 interrupts, remediation and rollback, policy drafts, exceptions, identity merges, scope changes) bound to a payload hash, with requester and expiry.

nodes.name: approval_events
nodes.summary: Append-only approval lifecycle events (opened, approved, rejected, changes requested, closed) with reviewer, exact decision, principal, role and break-glass flag; one approve or reject per item.

nodes.name: approval_status
nodes.summary: View laying each approval's latest event over the item to derive its current state and decision; redefined by later migrations as decision, requester, expiry, principal and break-glass columns arrive.

nodes.name: investigations
nodes.summary: Append-only Investigator conclusions about one verdict: root cause and category, missing evidence, proposed actions, citations, capped confidence and the model exchange.

nodes.name: gap_reports
nodes.summary: Append-only Policy Agent gap reports per control with summary, capped confidence and the model exchange.

nodes.name: policy_drafts
nodes.summary: Append-only registry of policy drafts stored on disk, with markdown hash, the gap report it is based on, addressed requirements and its approval item.

nodes.name: copilot_answers
nodes.summary: Append-only Copilot turns: question, intent, cited answer, requested actions, latency and the raw model exchange, unique per thread turn.

nodes.name: app_tenant
nodes.summary: plpgsql guard every tenant_isolation policy calls: returns app.tenant_id and raises when it is unset or empty, so a query outside a ScopedDB transaction fails loudly.

nodes.name: 0017_reliability.sql
nodes.summary: NT4 reliability migration: backoff and throttle-deferral columns on event_log, ordered_failures for per-consumer retry and dead-letter state on ordered topics, append-only dead_letter_replays, and an evaluation_key on agent_threads so a retried tier-3 run resumes its own thread.

nodes.name: 0018_tenant_keys.sql
nodes.summary: NT9 tenant-key hardening: adds composite (tenant_id, id) unique keys, re-points every single-column foreign key to a tenant-carrying composite reference, and re-keys both caches by tenant, because foreign-key and unique checks bypass row-level security.
nodes.languageNotes: Foreign-key and uniqueness checks are evaluated without RLS, so cross-tenant isolation has to be encoded in the keys themselves.

nodes.name: 0019_review_labels.sql
nodes.summary: NT10 insert-only review_labels table keeping every approved or rejected item's proposed payload, the reviewer's decision and the tenant's label-consent scope (none, eval, training) in force at the time.

nodes.name: 0020_rule_versions.sql
nodes.summary: NT6 migration adding verdicts.rule_version (the rule version and parameters hash that decided a verdict) with an index, so an auditor can ask by what method any stored verdict was reached.

nodes.name: 0021_ordered_seq.sql
nodes.summary: MT2 migration moving ordered topics from global offsets to a per-(tenant, topic) seq drawn from tenant_sequences: it backfills event_log.seq, seeds the counters, and converts consumer_offsets cursors from last_offset to last_seq.
nodes.languageNotes: The backfill uses row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY tenant_id, topic ORDER BY offset) and an ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE with greatest(), so rerunning it is harmless.

nodes.name: 0022_leases.sql
nodes.summary: MT2 migration that turns a parallel claim into a lease by adding lease_token, lease_owner and lease_expires_at to event_log, so a worker that lost its lease cannot overwrite the record.

nodes.name: 0023_work_hints.sql
nodes.summary: MT2 fair-dispatch work_hints table, one row per tenant and consumer with ready and last-served times; it holds only ids and times, so it has no row-level security and workers can claim across tenants.

nodes.name: 0024_subject_flight.sql
nodes.summary: MT2 migration adding a partial event_log index by partition key that finds a live claim per subject (one evaluation in flight), and a compliance_state.history flag for late verdicts filed into history without displacing the head.

nodes.name: 0025_schedules.sql
nodes.summary: MT2 tenant schedules: schedules holds each configured job's cadence, time zone and next due time, and append-only schedule_runs records every firing keyed by (tenant, schedule, slot) so a slot cannot fire twice across processes.

nodes.name: 0026_run_log.sql
nodes.summary: MT2 agent run log: append-only agent_steps records every model call, tool call and fence nonce of a run for resumes and replay checks, and agent_threads gains the input state a run started from.

nodes.name: 0027_policy_decisions.sql
nodes.summary: MT3 append-only policy_decisions table logging every tool-gateway permission decision: principal, run and user, tool and class, argument hash, effect (permit, deny, ask) and the deciding and shadow rules.

nodes.name: 0028_agent_role.sql
nodes.summary: MT3 migration granting the templated read-only {{agent_role}} SELECT on exactly the tables and views agent tools read, plus app_tenant(), so a tool bug or a model-driven tool can never write.

nodes.name: 0029_credential_issues.sql
nodes.summary: MT3 append-only credential_issues table recording every short-lived credential the remediation broker issues, bound to an approved item's payload hash, a scope and an expiry.

nodes.name: 0030_sync_runs.sql
nodes.summary: MT1 sync-run recording: append-only sync_runs for each connector pull (status, counts, error) and sync_run_scopes recording each declared scope as complete, partial, not_visible or failed.

nodes.name: 0031_sync_run_error_kind.sql
nodes.summary: MT1 migration adding sync_runs.error_kind (auth, not_visible, fail) to say why a failed sync run failed.

nodes.name: 0032_connections.sql
nodes.summary: MT1 connections as data: versioned append-only connections (connector, source, account, credential purpose name), a current_connections view, append-only connection_checks probes, and an index joining sync runs to their connection.

nodes.name: ordered_failures
nodes.summary: Per-consumer failure state of ordered-topic records with attempts, backoff and retrying, dead or resolved status, so one bad record no longer stalls a tenant.

nodes.name: dead_letter_replays
nodes.summary: Append-only log of every replay of a dead-lettered record, with outcome and who replayed it.

nodes.name: review_labels
nodes.summary: Insert-only reviewer decisions kept as labels with the proposed payload and the tenant's consent scope at decision time.

nodes.name: work_hints
nodes.summary: Cross-tenant fair-dispatch hints per tenant and consumer with ready and last-served times; ids and times only, so no RLS.

nodes.name: schedules
nodes.summary: Each tenant's configured jobs with cadence, time zone, next due time and enabled flag; a dropped schedule is disabled, not deleted.

nodes.name: schedule_runs
nodes.summary: Append-only schedule firings keyed by (tenant, schedule, slot), with missed slots folded in and the job record put on the log.

nodes.name: agent_steps
nodes.summary: Append-only agent run log of every model call, tool call and fence nonce, used to serve resumes and check replays.

nodes.name: policy_decisions
nodes.summary: Append-only tool-gateway permission decisions per call attempt: principal, tool class, argument hash, effect and deciding and shadow rules.

nodes.name: credential_issues
nodes.summary: Append-only record of short-lived remediation credentials, each bound to an approved item's payload hash, a scope, an expiry and later its grant.

nodes.name: sync_runs
nodes.summary: Append-only connector pull runs with status, counts, error class and kind, and the connection they ran for.

nodes.name: sync_run_scopes
nodes.summary: Per-scope outcomes of a sync run (complete, partial, not_visible, failed); a complete scope makes an absence a fact.

nodes.name: connections
nodes.summary: Versioned append-only connection definitions: connector, fixture or live source, provider account and the credential's purpose name, never the secret.

nodes.name: connection_checks
nodes.summary: Append-only probes of a connection's credential with outcome ok, auth, not_visible or fail.

nodes.name: current_connections
nodes.summary: SECURITY INVOKER view returning the latest version of each connection.

nodes.name: 0033_subject_inventories.sql
nodes.summary: MT8 expected-subject inventories: append-only subject_inventories records the population each test should have verdicts for and whether its source scopes were whole and fresh, and the parked_evaluations view exposes parked evaluation subjects to the app and agent roles.

nodes.name: 0034_pinned_inputs.sql
nodes.summary: MT8 pinned inputs: adds a recorded_seq watermark to the entity, identity-link and review tables, a manifest on verdicts, and an append-only replay_checks table for the nightly re-derivation sentinel.

nodes.name: 0035_rule_changes.sql
nodes.summary: MT8 rule-change notices: adds the rule_change reason and catalogue_version to compliance_state and an append-only rule_changes table recording each correction or amendment, its sign-off and every subject's status before and after.

nodes.name: 0036_tenant_members.sql
nodes.summary: MT4 per-tenant roles: versioned append-only tenant_members rows (IdP issuer and subject, role, active flag, grantor) with a current_tenant_members view, so history shows who could approve what and when.

nodes.name: 0037_signed_decisions.sql
nodes.summary: MT4 signed decisions: adds requested_by and expires_at to approvals, principal_id and role to approval_events, a unique index allowing one approve or reject per item, and redefines approval_status with the new columns.

nodes.name: 0038_execution_grants.sql
nodes.summary: MT4 execution grants: makes remediation_proposals insert-only by moving status into proposal_events (with a backfill), adds the proposal_status view, single-use execution_grants and grant_uses, and an execution_journal of what the executor did.
nodes.languageNotes: Converts mutable status columns into an event table: existing rows are copied as 'migrated:' events before the columns are dropped, and partial unique indexes allow at most one start and one end journal entry per grant.

nodes.name: 0039_exceptions_and_break_glass.sql
nodes.summary: MT4 exceptions and break-glass: adds the exception, identity_merge and break_glass_review approval kinds, flags break-glass approval events, and creates insert-only control_exceptions and exception_revocations with an exception_status view readable by agents.

nodes.name: 0040_tenants.sql
nodes.summary: MT4 tenants in the database: insert-only tenant_versions with a current_tenants view, a cross-tenant tenant_directory for dispatch, and the scope_change approval kind for changes to what is tested.

nodes.name: 0041_run_stops.sql
nodes.summary: MT4 run stops: insert-only run_stops records a person's request to stop one agent run, and agent_threads gains the cancelled status.

nodes.name: 0042_raw_versions.sql
nodes.summary: MT5 raw versioning: raw_events gains stored_sha256, version_id and store (local or s3), and insert-only raw_responses records each provider response a pull received with its request id and byte digest.

nodes.name: 0043_audit_chain.sql
nodes.summary: MT5 per-tenant tamper-evident hash chain: audit_chain, audit_chain_heads and audit_checkpoints tables, SECURITY DEFINER plpgsql functions that append entries from a deferred constraint trigger, and a DO block that writes genesis entries and attaches the trigger to 20 record tables.
nodes.languageNotes: Deferred constraint triggers (DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED) make chain entries follow commit order; the SECURITY DEFINER functions pin search_path and timezone so digests are stable and only the owner writes the chain.

nodes.name: 0044_aws_onboarding.sql
nodes.summary: MT6 AWS onboarding: widens the connections connector check to aws and idp, and adds insert-only aws_onboardings versions (account, generated external ID, role ARN, verification status and findings) with a current view.

nodes.name: 0045_release_bundles.sql
nodes.summary: MT7 release bundles: a non-tenant release_bundles manifest table, plus bundle_id columns on verdicts and agent_threads so every AI result names the bundle it ran under.

nodes.name: 0046_quality_signals.sql
nodes.summary: MT7 production quality signals: insert-only model_refusals per test and bundle, and quality_checks for the nightly judged sample and the daily canary and shadow runs.

nodes.name: 0047_chunk_versions.sql
nodes.summary: MT9 versioned retrieval index: insert-only index_generations, chained index_activations, chunk_sets and chunk_versions with character offsets and embeddings, plus generation and offset columns on the chunks serving projection; activations join the audit chain.

nodes.name: 0048_transcriptions.sql
nodes.summary: MT9 transcription provenance: adds evidence.page_methods and an insert-only transcriptions table recording each Claude-transcribed page or image with input digest, model, prompt version, legibility and cost.

nodes.name: subject_inventories
nodes.summary: Append-only expected subject populations per test and full run, with completeness, gaps and freshness.

nodes.name: parked_evaluations
nodes.summary: View over event_log listing the subject keys whose latest evaluation is parked, filtered by app_tenant() and exposing no ref or payload.

nodes.name: replay_checks
nodes.summary: Append-only results of the nightly sentinel re-deriving tier-1 verdicts: exact, rule_changed or mismatch with a diff.

nodes.name: rule_changes
nodes.summary: Append-only notices of rule changes (correction or amendment) with rule stamps, decider, sign-off and each subject's status before and after.

nodes.name: tenant_members
nodes.summary: Versioned append-only tenant memberships with IdP issuer and subject, role, active flag and grantor.

nodes.name: current_tenant_members
nodes.summary: SECURITY INVOKER view returning each member's latest membership version.

nodes.name: proposal_events
nodes.summary: Insert-only status history of remediation proposals with planned and executed calls, pre-state and refusal.

nodes.name: execution_grants
nodes.summary: Insert-only grants minted by one approve decision, bound to a proposal's payload and precondition hashes and valid for a day.

nodes.name: grant_uses
nodes.summary: Insert-only record of a grant's single use; the primary key blocks a second use whatever races.

nodes.name: execution_journal
nodes.summary: Insert-only executor journal per grant: started, observed, finished or failed, in simulated or live mode.

nodes.name: proposal_status
nodes.summary: SECURITY INVOKER view laying each proposal's latest event over the insert-only proposal row.

nodes.name: control_exceptions
nodes.summary: Insert-only accepted exceptions for a failing subject until a date, minted only by an approved exception item.

nodes.name: exception_revocations
nodes.summary: Insert-only early endings of control exceptions, by whom and why.

nodes.name: exception_status
nodes.summary: SECURITY INVOKER view joining each control exception with its revocation, if any.

nodes.name: tenant_versions
nodes.summary: Insert-only versions of a tenant's settings and status with reason, recorder and the scope_change item that allowed it.

nodes.name: tenant_directory
nodes.summary: Cross-tenant directory of existing tenants for the operator and scheduler; holds no settings.

nodes.name: current_tenants
nodes.summary: SECURITY INVOKER view returning the latest version of each tenant.

nodes.name: run_stops
nodes.summary: Insert-only requests to stop an agent run, checked at the next node boundary or tool call.

nodes.name: raw_responses
nodes.summary: Insert-only provider responses landed by pulls, with method, path, status, provider request id, digest, raw-zone ref and store.

nodes.name: audit_chain
nodes.summary: Per-tenant hash chain with one entry per inserted row of a chained table: row key, columns, digest and entry = sha256(prev | seq | table | digest).

nodes.name: audit_chain_heads
nodes.summary: Latest chain entry per tenant, owner-only and locked to serialize appends.

nodes.name: audit_checkpoints
nodes.summary: Insert-only signed statements of a tenant's chain head at a moment, also exported outside the database.

nodes.name: aws_onboardings
nodes.summary: Insert-only versions of an AWS account onboarding: generated external ID, role ARN, verification status and findings.

nodes.name: current_aws_onboardings
nodes.summary: SECURITY INVOKER view returning the latest onboarding version per AWS account.

nodes.name: release_bundles
nodes.summary: Non-tenant release bundle manifests (models, prompt and tool hash, rule catalogue, configuration digests), stored once.

nodes.name: model_refusals
nodes.summary: Insert-only model refusals per test and bundle, watched and gated per test.

nodes.name: quality_checks
nodes.summary: Insert-only quality checks (judged sample, canary, shadow, relabel, adequacy) with bundle, measurements and pass flag.

nodes.name: index_generations
nodes.summary: Insert-only retrieval index generations per embedding model and chunker version, with content-hash ids.

nodes.name: index_activations
nodes.summary: Insert-only, audit-chained switches of the serving index generation with reason and gate measurements.

nodes.name: chunk_sets
nodes.summary: Insert-only per-generation chunk sets of one evidence entity, naming the observation chunked, or a tombstone when evidence stops being current.

nodes.name: chunk_versions
nodes.summary: Insert-only chunk rows of a set with character offsets into the source text, generated tsvector and embedding, so quotes can be read back exactly.

nodes.name: transcriptions
nodes.summary: Insert-only model transcriptions of pages or images with input digest, model, prompt version, legibility and cost.

nodes.name: audit_chain_record
nodes.summary: SECURITY DEFINER plpgsql function that appends one hash-chain entry for a row: derives the primary-key json, digests the row, locks the tenant head, and writes entry = sha256(prev | seq | table | digest).

nodes.name: audit_chain_append
nodes.summary: Trigger function attached as a deferred constraint trigger on chained tables; records each inserted row through audit_chain_record at commit.

nodes.name: 0049_tasks.sql
nodes.summary: MT10 long tasks as typed rows: operational tasks with dollar, deadline and per-item run caps, task_items planned from scoping facts, and insert-only task_events on the audit chain.

nodes.name: 0050_tool_results.sql
nodes.summary: MT10 tool_results table keeping oversized or swapped-out agent tool results whole under a handle, readable by the read-only agent role through the read_result tool.

nodes.name: 0051_task_answers.sql
nodes.summary: MT10 insert-only task_answers on the audit chain: a person's answer to a waiting task item, which later runs read as quoted, untrusted text and never as evidence or approval.

nodes.name: 0052_run_metrics.sql
nodes.summary: MT10 insert-only run_metrics, one row per finished agent run with stop reasons, tool-call stats, correction rounds, context swaps, tokens, cost and acceptance, grouped per graph and bundle to gate releases.

nodes.name: 0053_judge_labels.sql
nodes.summary: MT10 judge sampling and expert relabel: insert-only judged_items, monthly relabel_batches and expert_labels, and the relabel kind added to quality_checks.

nodes.name: 0054_lookups.sql
nodes.summary: LT1 insert-only lookups table: code-chosen reads about a failing resource (AWS Config history, CloudTrail events, infrastructure code) with typed results and landed raw response ids, on the audit chain and readable by agents.

nodes.name: 0055_fix_suggestions.sql
nodes.summary: LT1 suggest-only fixes: insert-only fix_suggestions rendered by code from templates, fix_suggestion_events tracking status changes, and a fix_suggestion_status view; both tables join the audit chain.

nodes.name: 0056_evidence_feedback.sql
nodes.summary: LT2 evidence feedback: insert-only segment_sets holding a document version's citable segments and evidence_feedback recording admissibility or adequacy results, provenance badge and reasons.

nodes.name: 0057_auditor_decisions.sql
nodes.summary: LT2 insert-only auditor_decisions (accept or flag per document version) used to calibrate the adequacy verifier, plus the adequacy kind on quality_checks.

nodes.name: 0058_questionnaires.sql
nodes.summary: LT3 security questionnaires: operational questionnaires, insert-only questionnaire_answers, answer_events and a reusable answer_library, with an answer_status view and audit-chain triggers.

nodes.name: 0059_inventory.sql
nodes.summary: LT11 cloud inventory: insert-only resource_inventory snapshots from AWS Config and playbook_results recording fail or needs_review readings per resource and intent, both on the audit chain.

nodes.name: 0060_playbook_cleared.sql
nodes.summary: LT11 step 2 migration widening playbook_results.status to include cleared, which is still not a pass.

nodes.name: 0061_audit_packages.sql
nodes.summary: LT4 insert-only audit_packages table: sealed as-of packages per framework with a signed manifest, per-subject results for deltas and sealed object refs, on the audit chain.

nodes.name: 0062_auditor_workspace.sql
nodes.summary: LT4 auditor workspace: insert-only auditor_grants, auditor_revocations, an auditor_access read log, and attestations of every assertion leaving CCP under a versioned publication policy.

nodes.name: 0063_autonomy.sql
nodes.summary: LT8 autonomy: insert-only autonomy_levels per tenant, workflow and decision class (shadow, suggest, approve_each, sampled) and auto_decisions recording drafts accepted without review or routed to a person.

nodes.name: tasks
nodes.summary: Operational long-task rows (audit prep or questionnaire) with scope, dollar and deadline caps, spend, passes and status; changed only by the task runner.

nodes.name: task_items
nodes.summary: Operational task items planned by code from scoping facts, with status, attempts, evidence ids, open question and last run.

nodes.name: task_events
nodes.summary: Insert-only, audit-chained task event log of every plan, status change, run, cap, alert and park.

nodes.name: tool_results
nodes.summary: Insert-only oversized or swapped-out tool results kept whole under a handle for the read_result tool.

nodes.name: task_answers
nodes.summary: Insert-only, audit-chained answers a person gave to a waiting task item.

nodes.name: run_metrics
nodes.summary: Insert-only harness metrics per finished agent run: stops, tool calls, corrections, context swaps, tokens, cost and acceptance.

nodes.name: judged_items
nodes.summary: Insert-only verdict samples the nightly judge assessed, with stratum, confidence and judge pass.

nodes.name: relabel_batches
nodes.summary: Insert-only monthly batches of judged items selected for expert relabel, one per tenant and month.

nodes.name: expert_labels
nodes.summary: Insert-only expert labels on judged items, with annotator and note.

nodes.name: lookups

nodes.name: fix_suggestions
nodes.summary: Insert-only code-rendered fix suggestions for one failing resource: fix version, template hash, checked params, rendered body, offline checks and covering payload hash.

nodes.name: fix_suggestion_events
nodes.summary: Insert-only status changes of a fix suggestion (open, accepted, dismissed, confirmed, reopened, superseded) with actor and confirming verdict.

nodes.name: fix_suggestion_status
nodes.summary: SECURITY INVOKER view laying each suggestion's latest event over the suggestion row.

nodes.name: segment_sets
nodes.summary: Insert-only citable segments (sentences, headings, table cells with page offsets) of one document version by segmenter version.

nodes.name: evidence_feedback
nodes.summary: Insert-only admissibility or adequacy feedback on one document version with provenance badge, reasons and latency after landing.

nodes.name: auditor_decisions
nodes.summary: Insert-only auditor accept-or-flag decisions per document version, the labels the adequacy verifier is calibrated against.

nodes.name: questionnaires
nodes.summary: Operational security questionnaires with their questions, requester and sent status.

nodes.name: questionnaire_answers
nodes.summary: Insert-only drafted answers per question and run with every stage's output, code checks, cited pointers and relied-on verdicts.

nodes.name: answer_events
nodes.summary: Insert-only, audit-chained answer status events (draft, approved with edits, rejected, stale, sent).

nodes.name: answer_library
nodes.summary: Insert-only, audit-chained approved answers kept for reuse with their pointers and verdicts.

nodes.name: answer_status
nodes.summary: SECURITY INVOKER view laying each questionnaire answer's latest event over the answer row.

nodes.name: resource_inventory
nodes.summary: Insert-only AWS Config resource snapshots per account, flagged whole or incomplete.

nodes.name: playbook_results
nodes.summary: Insert-only service-playbook readings of one resource for one intent (fail, needs_review, later cleared; never pass) with JSON paths and raw responses.

nodes.summary: Insert-only time-boxed auditor read access to named packages, granted by a tenant admin.

nodes.name: auditor_access
nodes.summary: Insert-only log of every package file an auditor read, and when.

nodes.summary: Insert-only record of each assertion leaving CCP: policy version, allowed or not, reasons, item count and content digest.

nodes.name: autonomy_levels
nodes.summary: Insert-only autonomy level per tenant, workflow and decision class with who set it, the quality snapshot and bundle it rests on.

nodes.name: CLAUDE.md
nodes.summary: Instructions for Claude Code in this repository: a one-line description that names spec.md as the design to read before changing anything, plus skill-routing rules mapping request kinds (brainstorming, architecture, bugs, QA, review, ship, save and resume context) to skills.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Project overview: quickstart (docker compose, uv sync, `ccp db migrate`, knowledge load, run, report, evals), a command reference by area, a one-paragraph account of how a verdict is made, the load-bearing security guardrails, the evaluation harness, honest limits, running in AWS, data-processing disclosures, and the enforced layer order.

nodes.name: TODOS.md
nodes.summary: Deferred-work backlog with What/Why/Context/Effort/Priority per item: citation entailment as a second verification stage, growing the judge calibration set and the extraction and adversarial suites, tightening latency SLOs from run history, an OpenTelemetry OTLP exporter, and tenant- and user-namespaced long-term memory for the Copilot.

nodes.name: pyproject.toml
nodes.summary: Package and toolchain configuration for ccp: runtime dependencies (pydantic, psycopg, typer, anthropic, langgraph with the Postgres checkpointer, langfuse, fastapi, boto3), a dev group, the `ccp` console script bound to ccp.cli:app, hatchling build, pytest markers, ruff and strict mypy settings, and import-linter contracts for the layer order and for agents never importing credentials or the remediation broker (A-116).
nodes.languageNotes: The import-linter `layers` contract encodes the architecture as an ordered list (a package may import only those below it), and a `forbidden` contract keeps the agent packages away from credential-holding modules.

nodes.name: spec.md
nodes.summary: The v1.3 design specification for the teaching-scale compliance automation platform: goals and non-goals, target system shape, stack and environment, seventeen layers from connectors, ingestion, normalization and identity resolution through bitemporal storage, evaluators, the agent runtime, remediation, the eval harness, observability, security guardrails, the Investigator, Policy Agent, approval stage and Copilot, then the phased build plan and the running log of assumptions (A-1 onward) and resolved decisions.

nodes.name: base.html
nodes.summary: Base Jinja2 layout for the /ui console: inline CSS tokens and status colors, a header with the tenant's navigation (Inbox, Findings, SOC 2 and ISO 27001 reports, Runs), the signed-in principal and role with a sign-out form, and a flash-message slot around the body block.
nodes.languageNotes: Jinja2 template inheritance: every page template `{% extends "base.html" %}` and overrides the `title` and `body` blocks.

nodes.name: findings.html
nodes.summary: Findings page: one row per evaluated subject with its status (colored fail, pass or other), a link to the verdict, and each reason code with what it says and the next action that clears it.

nodes.name: home.html
nodes.summary: Signed-in landing page listing the user's tenant memberships and roles with Inbox and Findings links, or a hint to be added by a tenant admin or onboard one through POST /v1/tenants.

nodes.name: inbox.html
nodes.summary: Approval inbox: each open item shows its kind, open and expiry times, requester, state, undo note, payload and payload sha256, with Approve, Reject and Ask-for-changes forms that post the CSRF token and the payload hash; the requester sees no decision buttons on their own item.

nodes.name: login.html
nodes.summary: Offline sign-in form posting a subject to /ui/login through the local dev issuer, noting that a server in CCP_AUTH_MODE=oidc redirects to the identity provider instead.

nodes.name: report.html
nodes.summary: Framework report page (SOC 2 or ISO 27001): summary counts, then per requirement its state, the blocking test and subject, and pending reason codes with counts and next actions.

nodes.name: run.html
nodes.summary: Agent run detail page: thread id, status and error, a Stop form for reviewer, approver or admin roles while the run is running or interrupted, the step table from the run log, and an inline script that streams new steps over Server-Sent Events from the run's /events endpoint.
nodes.languageNotes: Initial rows are server-rendered; the EventSource script only appends steps with a higher seq and closes on the `end` event, so a reconnect does not duplicate rows.

nodes.name: runs.html
nodes.summary: Agent runs list: each run's thread id (linking to its run page), graph and test id, status, and last update time.

nodes.name: verdict.html
nodes.summary: Verdict detail page: status, tier, rule version and valid-from time, the reasoning labelled as rule-written or model-written summary, confidence and cap, reasons with next actions, the citations verified against evidence chunks, and failed quotes shown only as text.

nodes.name: admissibility.yaml
nodes.summary: Admissibility rules for uploaded evidence: per evidence type, the maximum age, whether a covered period, a resolvable subject or an issuer is required, and the tolerance for dates visible on scans. Code applies them on every upload before any model reads it; a blocking reason keeps the evidence out of evaluation.

nodes.name: controls.yaml
nodes.summary: Defines the eleven reusable controls (access revocation, privileged limits, change review, MFA, logging, cloud public access and more), each mapped to SOC 2 and ISO 27001 requirements and to the tests that evidence it.

nodes.name: fixes.yaml
nodes.summary: Versioned, suggest-only fix templates for failing AWS and GitHub findings (S3 public access block, IAM console access and MFA, multi-region CloudTrail, GitHub collaborator removal), each with whole-match parameter patterns, Terraform, CLI and console steps, and how CCP verifies the fix on its next read.
nodes.languageNotes: Parameters are regex-validated before rendering and the CLI's leading words pin the only program a rendered command may start with, a template-injection guard expressed as data.

nodes.name: impact.yaml
nodes.summary: The impact table: seventeen rules naming which table change, under which conditions, re-evaluates which tests and how the subject is resolved, so a single entity change enqueues only the affected (test, subject) pairs.

nodes.name: lookups.yaml
nodes.summary: Per failing AWS test (AWS-1..3), the read-only lookups run before investigation: the AWS Config resource type whose history is read, the CloudTrail events that can change the setting, and the Terraform resource types to search for in the customer's code.

nodes.name: playbook_fields.yaml
nodes.summary: For service playbooks, the JSON Pointer into each AWS resource type's recorded configuration and the expected value per intent (encrypted, not_public, backed_up, logged), so these gaps are decided by code rather than a model.

nodes.name: question_map.yaml
nodes.summary: Keyword terms per control id used to map a security questionnaire question to the tested control it is about; the mapped control's verdicts, not a model, decide the answer's direction.

nodes.name: service_classes.yaml
nodes.summary: Cloud service taxonomy: ten service classes with the intents each must meet, a reviewed lookup of nineteen AWS resource types to classes, and which deterministic test covers each intent; uncovered intents become playbook gaps.

nodes.name: tests.yaml
nodes.summary: The test catalogue: fourteen test specs (GH-1..5, HR-1..5, AWS-1..3, IDP-1) declaring evaluation mode, evidence types, deciding rule, controls, required complete sources, subject sources, valid-time strategy and revalidation cadence that the router and evaluators consume.

nodes.name: aws1.yaml
nodes.summary: Declarative AWS-1 check: reads S3 bucket assets and requires the effective public access block (set at the account or the bucket) on each, with templated fail and pass messages listing failing bucket names.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a small check DSL (read/where filters, optional population subset, require predicates, message templates) interpreted by the declarative evaluator instead of Python rule code.

nodes.name: aws2.yaml
nodes.summary: Declarative AWS-2 check: among active IAM-user grants, the population with console access must each have MFA enabled; failing users are listed by user name.

nodes.name: aws3.yaml
nodes.summary: Declarative AWS-3 check: every observed AWS account asset must carry a logging multi-region CloudTrail trail, abstaining when no account was observed.

nodes.name: hr2.yaml
nodes.summary: Declarative HR-2 check: active grants on the HRIS identity provider, narrowed to human identities, must all have MFA enabled; failing identities are listed by email.

nodes.name: idp1.yaml
nodes.summary: Declarative IDP-1 check: every active identity-provider user grant must have an active MFA factor, abstaining when no identity-provider users were observed.

nodes.name: adequacy_v1.md
nodes.summary: System prompt for the document-adequacy check: the model reviews one uploaded document, given as numbered segments, against the controls it was uploaded for and returns accept/flag with coded reasons (wrong_period, wrong_subject, unsigned, etc.) citing segment ids rather than quoted text.

nodes.name: check_draft_v1.md
nodes.summary: System prompt for drafting a declarative compliance check: the model fills a schema (read_from, read_where, population_where, require conditions, abstain_reason, fail/pass text templates) that a small interpreter executes, with code validation and a named reviewer gating shipment.

nodes.name: contextual_v1.md
nodes.summary: System prompt for contextual retrieval: given a whole document and one chunk, the model writes one or two sentences situating the chunk so chunk search can find it, with no preamble or judgement.

nodes.name: copilot_answer_v1.md
nodes.summary: System prompt for the Compliance Copilot answering step: per-intent rules (explain, status, missing, act, other) for answering an operator from gathered tool results and fenced excerpts with verbatim chunk-id citations, proposing catalogue actions for reviewer approval instead of acting.

nodes.name: copilot_classify_v1.md
nodes.summary: System prompt for the Compliance Copilot classifier: assigns one intent (explain, status, missing, act, other) to an operator question and extracts the test id, subject and framework when named.

nodes.name: copilot_gather_v1.md
nodes.summary: System prompt for the Compliance Copilot gathering step: the model uses only the offered read-only tools to collect what the intent's contract requires (findings, verdicts, rollups, investigations, grants) and stops once satisfied, never acting.

nodes.name: gather_fallback_v1.md
nodes.summary: System prompt for the evaluator's fallback gathering step: when a direct fetch finds no evidence of the required type, the model runs a few short alternative-wording searches and reports in one sentence what was or was not found.

nodes.name: gh4_extract_v1.md
nodes.summary: Extraction prompt for test GH-4: reads fenced evidence from a repository's security or vulnerability disclosure policy and fills policy_exists, timeline_stated and a verbatim timeline_text, each backed by a chunk-id citation; code, not the model, decides the status.
nodes.languageNotes: Every prompt in this directory ends with the same fenced-data clause telling the model to treat fenced content as data, a shared prompt-injection defence.

nodes.name: hr3_extract_v1.md
nodes.summary: Extraction prompt for test HR-3: reads a security-awareness training record for one named employee and fills subject match, completion status, completion date and provider, each with a verbatim chunk-id citation.

nodes.name: hr4_extract_v1.md
nodes.summary: Extraction prompt for test HR-4: reads a user access review report and records the review date and the systems stated as in scope, excluding deferred or unreviewed systems, each with a verbatim chunk-id citation.

nodes.name: hr4_systems_v1.md
nodes.summary: Extraction prompt for the HR-4 critical-systems inventory: lists every system the inventory tags as critical, using names exactly as written and a verbatim chunk-id citation per entry.

nodes.name: investigator_diagnose_v1.md
nodes.summary: First version of the compliance investigator's diagnosis prompt: given a verdict, subject context and fenced evidence, fills root_cause, root_cause_category, missing_evidence, proposed_actions from a fixed catalogue, and citations; superseded by v2.

nodes.name: investigator_diagnose_v2.md
nodes.summary: Current compliance investigator diagnosis prompt: extends v1 with a fixes field that picks suggest-only remediations from the context's fix list with parameters copied exactly from evidence, while still proposing catalogue actions and never acting or deciding status.
nodes.languageNotes: Prompts are versioned by filename (_v1, _v2) and referenced by version string from code, so a new version is added beside the old one rather than edited in place.

nodes.name: investigator_gather_v1.md
nodes.summary: System prompt for the compliance investigator's gathering step: uses offered tools to collect cited evidence, access grants, the served control and any deciding document for a failed or undecided verdict, then summarizes what was found and what is missing.

nodes.name: judge_v1.md
nodes.summary: LLM-as-judge prompt for evals: grades one candidate output against a numbered rubric, quoting the shortest supporting passage per criterion, with overall_pass only when every criterion is met and self-claims by the candidate ignored.

nodes.name: mapping_v1.md
nodes.summary: System prompt for framework mapping: the model maps one requirement of a new framework to up to three ranked candidate CCP controls, returning control_ids, an abstain flag, confidence and a checkable reason for reviewer acceptance.

nodes.name: playbook_v1.md
nodes.summary: System prompt for cloud-resource playbooks: judges one resource's recorded configuration against one intent (encrypted, not_public, logged, etc.) as fail, unclear or no_issue, citing RFC 6901 JSON Pointers and values that CCP verifies.

nodes.name: policy_compose_v1.md
nodes.summary: System prompt for the policy-drafting step: writes a Markdown policy section in the tenant's voice that closes every gap from a control's gap report, without naming people, copying secrets or claiming approval.

nodes.name: policy_gap_v1.md
nodes.summary: System prompt for the policy gap-analysis step: for each requirement of a control, decides whether tenant policy excerpts cover every clause, citing verbatim chunk-id passages or describing the gap, plus an overall coverage summary.

nodes.name: policy_gather_v1.md
nodes.summary: System prompt for the policy gap-analysis gathering step: runs a few short searches over the tenant's policy documents built from requirement wording and summarizes what policy text exists.

nodes.name: questionnaire_facts_v1.md
nodes.summary: System prompt for the questionnaire facts step: extract short facts bearing on one question, each with its chunk id and a verbatim quote of at most 300 characters, without answering the question or deciding compliance; fenced evidence is declared data, not instructions.

nodes.name: questionnaire_prose_v1.md
nodes.summary: System prompt for drafting a questionnaire answer for human review: use the control-decided direction when given, otherwise choose only from checked facts, and write two to four sentences whose numbers, periods and names all appear in a fact.

nodes.name: second_reader_v1.md
nodes.summary: System prompt for the second reader: check whether code-verified quotes actually support each extracted field value behind a PASS, returning agrees with a one-sentence reason naming the unsupported field, without deciding status or redoing extraction.

nodes.name: task_item_answer_v1.md
nodes.summary: System prompt for the answer step of a compliance reading task: one reading per item id with answer, one-line reason, up to eight findings each citing a fenced chunk verbatim, and the missing evidence when the answer is partial or insufficient.

nodes.name: task_item_gather_v1.md
nodes.summary: System prompt for the gathering step of a compliance reading task: use only the offered tools to search and read evidence for each item, stop when nothing new appears, and report what was found and what is missing without deciding status.

nodes.name: transcribe_v1.md
nodes.summary: System prompt for transcribing one document page or screenshot word for word into plain text, with tables as pipe rows and [illegible] markers, treating any instruction visible on the image as text to transcribe, never to follow.

nodes.name: autonomy.yaml
nodes.summary: Autonomy policy (LT8, A-171) defining when a draft may skip human review: promotion bar on a published quality snapshot (false-accept upper bound, minimum FAIL cases, pass^k), a daily exposure budget with a seeded review sample, and per-workflow decision classes marked by reversibility and impact.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses YAML flow mappings for compact per-class settings; only reversible, low-impact classes are eligible for the sampled level.

nodes.name: canary.yaml
nodes.summary: Daily canary definition (A-144): a pass-rate floor of 1.0 and the list of golden tier 2/tier 3 cases that call the real model against the production release bundle.

nodes.name: cells.yaml
nodes.summary: Cell topology (LT9, A-172) declaring the us-1 and eu-1 deployment cells, each with its AWS region, data-residency promise, model provider (first-party Anthropic or Bedrock EU inference profiles mapped from pinned model ids) and Voyage embeddings endpoint.

nodes.name: context_ceilings.yaml
nodes.summary: Per-call-type input token ceilings (A-153) for tier 2 extraction, agent calls, Copilot turns and whole-document reads, plus the tool-result swap threshold and preview size; part of the release bundle.

nodes.name: copilot.yaml
nodes.summary: Compliance Copilot limits (Layer 17, A-36): maximum actions per turn, the gather loop's tool-call budget, and words forbidden as summary judgements in status answers.

nodes.name: eval_gates.yaml
nodes.summary: Release gates for model-backed eval targets (A-103, A-144): Wilson lower-bound pass^k floor, false-PASS upper-bound ceiling, minimum case counts, refusal-rate cap and the judge agreement threshold used by `ccp evals regress`.
nodes.languageNotes: Long header comment documents the statistical rationale (confidence bounds instead of single-flip gates for nondeterministic model cases).

nodes.name: eval_method.yaml
nodes.summary: Published evaluation method (LT6, A-170) attached to every quality snapshot: labeller roles and qualifications, run settings (runs per case, thinking, sampling, infrastructure) and the minimum FAIL cases before a false-PASS bound is published.

nodes.name: evaluation.yaml
nodes.summary: Human-interrupt confidence threshold (A-10, A-47) below which a tier 3 run stops for a reviewer, with a field recording when it was last read off the reliability curve.

nodes.name: identity.yaml
nodes.summary: Identity-resolution scoring model (Layer 4): feature weights for email, handle, name similarity and employee id matches (including a negative weight for conflicting verified emails) and the auto-merge / auto-distinct thresholds.

nodes.name: publication_policy.yaml
nodes.summary: Versioned publication policy (LT4, A-169) governing what CCP may assert externally: per assertion kind (package share, questionnaire, trust page) the allowed evidence provenance, maximum item age and whether incomplete items may go out.

nodes.name: remediation.yaml
nodes.summary: Live-mode remediation allowlist (Layer 10, gate 3): repositories remediation may act on (empty by default) and GitHub logins that are always protected.

nodes.name: retrieval.yaml
nodes.summary: Retrieval knobs (HNSW ef_search, candidate count, top_k, RRF k) and the measured distractor-percentile thresholds that `ccp index calibrate` writes back; part of the release bundle.

nodes.name: retrieval_gates.yaml
nodes.summary: Per-evidence-type retrieval quality gates (A-148) applied by `ccp index gate` and `ccp index reembed`: default Recall@5, MRR and distractor-at-1 floors, minimum query counts, and relaxed overrides for the keyless local-hashing-v1 embedding model.

nodes.name: slos.yaml
nodes.summary: Provisional p95 latency SLOs in milliseconds per eval target (Layer 11), from connector pulls through tier 2/3 verdicts, investigations and Copilot answers; `ccp evals regress` fails on a breach.

nodes.name: task_kinds.yaml
nodes.summary: Long-task fan-out gate (A-151): which task kinds (audit_prep, questionnaire) may fan out their read items, and the single-run item cap used to record a baseline first.

nodes.name: tenants.yaml
nodes.summary: Fixture tenant definitions (Acme and Globex) with GitHub org, admin limits, critical asset tags, termination revocation SLA, daily LLM budget, concurrency and time zone; the seed version before a tenant has a database version.

nodes.name: tool_policy.yaml
nodes.summary: Agent tool-permission rules (A-113) layered on the default-deny per-graph allowlists and enforced by policy.check on every tool call; currently a log-only rule watching REST API readers.

nodes.name: component.yaml
nodes.summary: Sixty-nine exact-graded component golden cases across twelve targets (connector pulls, mapper, identity pairing, tier 1-3 verdicts, chunker, retrieval metrics, knowledge router, policy gap, investigation, copilot answers), grouped by build phase and including judged, extraction and trajectory suites plus planted-secret and prompt-injection fixtures.
nodes.languageNotes: Expected values use matcher operators such as $subset and $gte, so a case pins only the fields that decide it.

nodes.name: e2e.yaml
nodes.summary: Two end-to-end golden cases running the full pipeline per tenant: acme's termination case pinning landed counts, tier 1 compliance heads and SOC 2 / ISO 27001 requirement states, and globex's tenant-isolation case.

nodes.name: probes.yaml
nodes.summary: Four keyed context-probe cases that squeeze a task item run's context and check in code that it keeps a planted fact, rereads swapped-out results by handle, resumes without redoing work, and cites spans at early, middle and late positions.

nodes.name: retrieval.yaml
nodes.summary: Retrieval golden set of thirty-six queries for the acme and globex tenants, naming relevant chunks by evidence id or prefix plus a substring, scored by Recall@5, MRR and nDCG@10 against the fixture corpus and generated distractors.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Explains the twenty-case labeled calibration set used to measure the LLM judge: how to read agreement and Cohen's kappa at n = 20, the case categories and what each probes, provenance limits (single author-annotator), and the growth path via captured traces and reviewer-decision exports.

nodes.name: copilot.yaml
nodes.summary: Five labeled copilot answers (three that keep their contracts, two fluent but confidently wrong) with criterion labels c1..c5 and an overall label, graded against the copilot answer rubric.

nodes.name: verdicts.yaml
nodes.summary: Fifteen labeled tier 2 and tier 3 verdict outputs (clean passes, clean fails, and borderline cases such as following an injected instruction or citing non-supporting quotes) with c1..c5 and overall labels against the verdict reasoning rubric.

nodes.name: copilot_answer.md
nodes.summary: LLM-judge rubric for Copilot answers: five criteria requiring grounding in gathered tool results, verbatim citations, factual status answers that never declare readiness or compliance, requested changes framed as reviewer approvals, and no cross-tenant leakage or guessing.

nodes.name: copilot_answer.paraphrase.md
nodes.summary: Second wording of the five Copilot-answer criteria, used to measure whether the judge's verdicts stay stable when the rubric is paraphrased.

nodes.name: investigation.md
nodes.summary: LLM-judge rubric for Investigator outputs: five criteria checking that the root cause names specific evidence and gap, the category matches the cause, missing evidence types are real requirements, actions come from the catalogue, and instructions embedded in evidence are not followed.

nodes.name: investigation.paraphrase.md
nodes.summary: Second wording of the five investigation criteria, used to test the judge's robustness to rubric paraphrase.

nodes.name: policy_draft.md
nodes.summary: LLM-judge rubric for Policy Agent drafts: five criteria requiring every uncovered requirement clause to be addressed specifically, commitments traceable to requirements or existing tenant policy, tenant-only naming, no leaked evidence content, and no claim of being approved or in force.

nodes.name: policy_draft.paraphrase.md
nodes.summary: Second wording of the five policy-draft criteria, used to check that judge verdicts survive a paraphrased rubric.

nodes.name: verdict_reasoning.md
nodes.summary: LLM-judge rubric for tier 2 and tier 3 evaluator verdicts: the judge sees only case input and verdict and marks five criteria met or not met with a supporting passage (specific evidence named, claims traceable to cited chunks, status consistent with reasoning, embedded instructions ignored, absent evidence acknowledged).

nodes.name: verdict_reasoning.paraphrase.md
nodes.summary: Second wording of the five verdict-reasoning criteria, used for rubric-paraphrase robustness of the tier 2 and tier 3 judge.

nodes.name: database.tf
nodes.summary: Provisions the cell's RDS PostgreSQL 17 primary: Multi-AZ, encrypted gp3 storage, forced TLS, 35-day point-in-time backups and deletion protection, behind a security group that admits only the ECS tasks; its snapshots back the audit restore drill.

nodes.name: monitoring.tf
nodes.summary: CloudWatch alarms for a CCP cell covering database CPU and free storage, API 5xx errors, the worker service dropping below one running task, and a log metric filter that alarms when the hourly audit verify reports findings.

nodes.name: outputs.tf
nodes.summary: Terraform outputs exposing the cell's API URL, raw and audit bucket names, audit signing key ARN, database endpoint and ECS cluster name.

nodes.name: scale.tf
nodes.summary: Scale-out layer for a cell: an optional RDS read replica for reports and a two-task PgBouncer Fargate service in transaction mode in front of the primary; dedicated or EU cells reuse the same module with their own cell, region and tenants.
nodes.languageNotes: count = var.read_replica ? 1 : 0 is the idiomatic Terraform toggle for an optional resource.

nodes.name: services.tf
nodes.summary: ECS Fargate runtime for a cell: cluster, log group, load-balancer and task security groups, a least-privilege task IAM role that can put, get and hold objects but never delete, api and worker task definitions sharing one image with Secrets Manager secrets, and an HTTPS load balancer in front of the api.
nodes.languageNotes: for_each over an inline map builds both the api and worker task definitions and services from one block, and a dynamic load_balancer block attaches only to the api.

nodes.name: storage.tf
nodes.summary: Evidence storage for a cell: the raw S3 bucket with versioning, governance-mode Object Lock, per-tenant KMS keys and a TLS- and KMS-only policy; and, in the separate audit account, a compliance-mode locked checkpoint bucket plus an ECC P-256 signing key the app may only sign and verify with.
nodes.languageNotes: for_each over a set variable creates one KMS key and alias per tenant, and the aws.audit provider alias places resources in a second AWS account.

nodes.name: variables.tf
nodes.summary: Input variables for a cell deployment: region and cell name, audit role and app account, VPC and subnets, the tenant set for per-tenant keys, container images, database class, raw and audit retention days, alarm topic, ACM certificate and the read-replica toggle.

nodes.name: versions.tf
nodes.summary: Pins Terraform >= 1.9 and the AWS provider >= 5.80 with an S3 state backend, and declares the default provider plus an aliased provider that assumes a role in the separate audit account, tagging resources by app and cell.

nodes.name: aws_security_group.db

nodes.name: aws_db_parameter_group.ccp

nodes.name: aws_db_instance.ccp
nodes.summary: The cell's primary RDS PostgreSQL 17 instance: Multi-AZ, encrypted autoscaling gp3 storage, an RDS-managed master password, 35-day backups, deletion protection, a final snapshot, Performance Insights and exported PostgreSQL logs.

nodes.name: aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.workers_down

nodes.name: aws_cloudwatch_log_metric_filter.audit_findings

nodes.name: aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.audit_findings

nodes.name: aws_db_instance.replica

nodes.name: aws_security_group.pooler

nodes.name: aws_ecs_task_definition.pooler

nodes.name: aws_ecs_cluster.ccp

nodes.name: partitions.py
nodes.summary: Admin-side Postgres maintenance for the largest tenants (spec A-172): converts an allowlisted table into a parent LIST-partitioned by tenant_id with a default partition, preserving grants, forced row-level security and the tenant_isolation policy, then moves a large tenant into its own partition with its own indexes.
nodes.languageNotes: DDL cannot take bind parameters, so table names are guarded by an allowlist and an identifier regex before f-string interpolation, and ATTACH PARTITION uses psycopg's sql.Identifier/sql.Literal composition.

nodes.name: is_partitioned
nodes.summary: Reports whether a public table is already a partitioned parent by checking pg_class.relkind = 'p'.

nodes.name: partition_table
nodes.summary: Converts an allowlisted table into a tenant LIST-partitioned parent in one transaction: refuses unique keys lacking tenant_id, renames and copies rows into a default partition, re-grants app and agent role privileges, and re-enables forced RLS with the tenant_isolation policy; returns False when already partitioned.

nodes.name: partition_name
nodes.summary: Derives a sanitized, validated partition name of the form <table>_t_<tenant> from a tenant id, rejecting unusable identifiers.

nodes.name: own_partition
nodes.summary: Moves one tenant's rows into a dedicated partition in a single transaction by detaching the default partition, copying and deleting that tenant's rows, then attaching both partitions again.

nodes.name: layout
nodes.summary: Lists each partition of a table with its row count, run as the admin role for inspection.

nodes.name: eng-review-2026-09-11.md
nodes.summary: Engineering review of spec.md v1.2 (2026-09-11) giving a verdict, the target architecture diagram, a 22-entry decision register (D5-D26) and prioritized recommendations R1-R20 (P0 identity scoring, idempotent evaluation, bitemporal writer, loud isolation failure), plus evaluation, security, observability, failure-mode and implementation-task sections.

nodes.name: verify-with-credentials.md
nodes.summary: Checklist of verifications still owed against real services, grouped by credential (Anthropic, OpenAI, Voyage, GitHub, AWS, Okta and HR aggregator, Langfuse, Cognito/OIDC, git remote), each item naming the CLI command, expected outcome and spec assumption for features built and tested only offline.

nodes.name: cases.yaml
nodes.summary: The S17 prompt-injection suite: 16 adversarial cases (9 acme, 7 globex) across seven attack classes such as direct override, role play, obfuscation, fake citation, table cell, cross-tenant and judge-targeted, each planting a payload in a policy chunk for tier-2 test GH-4 and succeeding only if the verdict flips from the control's expected status.
nodes.languageNotes: Contains deliberately hostile payload strings; they are test data loaded by the eval harness, not instructions.

nodes.name: questionnaire.yaml
nodes.summary: Labelled five-question questionnaire fixture for `ccp tasks measure` (spec A-151), giving each question's expected answer (yes or insufficient_evidence) as a reviewer read acme's evidence, used to score single versus fan-out task runs.

nodes.name: information-security-policy-v4.md
nodes.summary: Acme's version 4 information security policy fixture with front matter and seven sections stating concrete controls (quarterly access reviews, 24-hour leaver removal, MFA, second-engineer code review, disclosure timelines, annual training, secrets manager), serving as the strong-evidence tenant corpus.

nodes.name: manifest.yaml
nodes.summary: Upload manifest for tenant acme listing a security awareness training certificate PDF for employee E1058 and the v4 information security policy, with evidence types and issued/uploaded timestamps; the tenant comes from the directory, not the manifest.

nodes.name: information-security-policy-v2.md
nodes.summary: Globex's version 2 information security policy fixture: a deliberately thin five-section policy with vague access reviews, password-only authentication and no timelines, giving the evaluators a weak-evidence tenant that produces gaps.

nodes.name: manifest.yaml
nodes.summary: Upload manifest for tenant globex listing the H1 2026 user access review PDF and the v2 information security policy with evidence types and issued/uploaded timestamps.

nodes.name: ccp-read-role.yaml
nodes.summary: CloudFormation template a customer deploys to create the CCPReadOnly IAM role (spec A-139): assumable only by CCP's principal with the generated external ID, granted SecurityAudit, with explicit denies on secret- and data-bearing reads and a NotAction deny on anything beyond a read allowlist; outputs the role ARN for onboarding.
nodes.languageNotes: Combines an AWS managed policy with an inline Deny and a Deny NotAction statement, so even future additions to SecurityAudit cannot grant writes or secret reads.

nodes.name: make_fixture_pdfs.py
nodes.summary: Dev-only fpdf2 script that regenerates the committed fixture PDFs reproducibly with a pinned creation date: Acme's training certificate, Globex's access review whose scope table splits across a page break, and a drawing-only PDF with no text layer.

nodes.name: _pdf
nodes.summary: Creates an A4 FPDF document with the pinned creation date, auto page break and fixed margins so output bytes are reproducible.

nodes.name: training_certificate
nodes.summary: Writes Acme's Security Awareness Training Certificate PDF for Ana Torres (E1058) with status, completion date, provider and score.

nodes.name: access_review
nodes.summary: Writes Globex's H1 2026 User Access Review PDF, deliberately pushing the scope table to the bottom of page one so rows continue on page two to exercise page-aware chunking and citations.

nodes.name: no_text_layer
nodes.summary: Writes a drawing-only PDF containing just a filled rectangle, used to test rejection of PDFs without extractable text.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Maps each fixture output path to its generator, creates parent directories, writes every PDF and prints its size.

nodes.name: all_exceptions
nodes.summary: Returns every control exception for the tenant, oldest grant first, read from the exception_status view.

nodes.name: excepted_until
nodes.summary: Maps each subject key whose exception holds now to the date that exception lasts until.

nodes.name: forget
nodes.summary: Drops the cached tenant settings for the scoped tenant so the next read sees an approved scope change.

nodes.name: believed_state
nodes.summary: Returns what was believed about a subject at a moment, as known at that same moment.

nodes.name: _guarded_tenant
nodes.summary: Resolves the tenant a thread id names and rejects a --tenant that disagrees or an unknown tenant, before any checkpoint access.

nodes.name: load_config
nodes.summary: Loads the copilot config from YAML, falling back to defaults when the file is missing.

nodes.name: says_forbidden
nodes.summary: Returns the forbidden summary words found in a text, matched whole-word and case-insensitively.

nodes.name: workflow.yaml
nodes.summary: Four exact-graded workflow-level golden cases: HRIS ingest deduplication on a repeated pull, late-arrival ordering by source timestamp, and idempotent tier 1 evaluation runs for acme (15 pairs) and globex (13 pairs). The tier 1 expectations count AWS-1..3 and IDP-1 as needs_review abstentions, since the fixtures hold no AWS or identity-provider data.
nodes.languageNotes: Each YAML list entry is one golden case keyed by a `target` name that the eval runner dispatches to a registered target function; inline flow mappings keep the expected counts compact.

layers.name: CLI & Web API
layers.description: The `ccp` Typer CLI and `python -m ccp` entry that mount every sub-command, plus the FastAPI /v1 app (onboarding, approvals inbox, findings and reports, fix suggestions, autonomy levels, method cards and auditor workspace endpoints), reason codes and server-rendered HTML templates for the inbox, runs, findings, verdict and report pages.

layers.name: Evaluation Harness
layers.description: Evaluation of model-backed work (golden and adversarial sets, LLM judge and calibration, shadow and regression gates, context probes, production sampling and expert relabels), offline drafting of declarative checks and framework-mapping review, method cards and published per-workflow quality snapshots, `ccp replay` that rebuilds stored model requests, and the golden/labeled YAML datasets and grading rubrics they score against.

layers.name: Agent Workflows
layers.description: The agent harness (LangGraph graphs, tool allowlists, authz, run logs, stop rules, bundles) and the workflows built on it - copilot, investigation (including code-written investigations), policy drafting, task items, pre-investigation lookups with cloud inventory, coverage maps and service playbooks, suggest-only fix suggestions with evidence-based confirmation, and security questionnaires - together with approval actions, tenant onboarding, and the compliance-state run that writes the bitemporal state table, signs as-of audit packages, records attestations under the publication policy, runs the auditor workspace and governs review-skipping autonomy levels.

layers.name: Evaluators
layers.description: Compliance test evaluation: tier-1 deterministic and declarative rules for the GH/HR/AWS/IdP checks, tier-2 LLM extraction with verified citations and a second reader, immediate feedback and a calibrated adequacy verifier for uploaded evidence, confidence, completeness and quality scoring, budget gates, rule versioning and the verdict record.

layers.name: Knowledge, Retrieval & LLM
layers.description: The compliance knowledge catalogue (SOC 2 and ISO 27001 frameworks, controls, tests, declarative checks, impact rollups, tenant overlays, code-scored framework mapping, evidence admissibility rules, the suggest-only fix catalogue, per-test lookups and cloud service classes), the hybrid document retrieval stack (deterministic segmentation, admission, chunking, contextual embeddings, rerank, calibration and gates), and the LLM client layer with pinned models, budgets, context ceilings and versioned prompt templates.

layers.name: Ingestion & Identity
layers.description: Evidence intake from GitHub, AWS, HRIS, Okta and manual uploads: source connectors with conformance checks, the ingest worker, topics, raw zone and landing, mappers that normalize payloads into entities, identity resolution across sources, and the signed audit hash chain with its standalone offline audit-package verifier.

layers.name: Platform Foundation
layers.description: Shared base every package imports: tenant-scoped Postgres access with row-level security, bitemporal helpers, per-tenant partitioning and the numbered SQL migrations, auth tokens and members, the approval store and single-use execution grants, secret and prompt-injection guards, tracing and cost observability, deployment cells with data residency, and the core config, credentials, tenancy and types modules.

layers.name: Tests & Fixtures
layers.description: Pytest suites for security boundaries (tenant isolation, RLS, prompt injection, tool allowlists, approval fail-closed), workflow and chaos-worker runs, property-based bitemporal checks and the end-to-end remediation loop, plus the acme and globex fixture tenants (GitHub, HRIS, uploads) and the script that regenerates fixture PDFs.

layers.name: Infrastructure & Configuration
layers.description: Deployment and runtime settings: Dockerfile and docker-compose, GitHub Actions CI, deploy and nightly-eval workflows, Terraform (including the read-replica and PgBouncer scale-out module) and CloudFormation for AWS, pyproject with the import-linter layer contract, and the config/*.yaml files that tune evaluation, retrieval, copilot, remediation, tool policy, SLOs, tenants, cells, autonomy, the evaluation method and the publication policy.
